Gochujang Bulgogi Beef Bowls with Chili Onion Crunch
🍚
Gochujang Bulgogi Beef Bowls with Chili Onion Crunch
Weeknight dinner · Korean · 25 min · 2 servings
♡

Sticky-sweet, deeply browned beef over hot jasmine rice, finished with a runny fried egg and a spoonful of crackling chili onion crunch.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
?
Swap: No Crunchy Chili Onion on the shelf? A spoon of Fusia sriracha plus a scatter of fried onions gets you the same heat-and-crunch effect.
Leftovers: Keep the beef separate from the rice in the fridge for up to three days and reheat it in a hot skillet so the glaze re-caramelizes.
Carne Asada Tacos with Charred Peppers and Chili Lime Crema
🌮
Carne Asada Tacos with Charred Peppers and Chili Lime Crema
Weeknight dinner · Mexican · 30 min · 2 servings
♡

Hard-seared marinated steak sliced thin and piled into blistered tortillas with smoky peppers, salsa verde, and a tangy chili lime crema.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
?
?
?
Swap: If the Carne Asada Autentica is sold out, Aldi flank steak rubbed with Chili Lime Seasoning and lime juice works just as hard.
Leftovers: Chop leftover steak and peppers together and fold them into scrambled eggs or a protein wrap for a fast next-day breakfast burrito.
Thai Red Curry Shrimp with Blistered Green Beans
🍤
Thai Red Curry Shrimp with Blistered Green Beans
Weeknight dinner · Thai · 25 min · 2 servings
♡

Plump red shrimp poached in a coconut-rich red curry that is sweet, salty, and lime-sharp all at once, spooned over jasmine rice.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
Swap: Yellow Curry Sauce makes a milder, more golden version, and Season's Choice frozen green beans stand in for the shiitake ones.
Leftovers: The curry thickens overnight, so reheat it gently with a splash of water and add the shrimp back only at the very end.

🍲
Harissa Chicken and Chickpea Tagine with Apricots
Big batch cook · Moroccan · 70 min · 6 servings
♡

Fall-apart chicken thighs braised with harissa, warm cinnamon, and sweet dried apricots until the whole pot tastes like a spice market.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: Zhoug Sauce stirred in at the end brings a green, herby heat if Harissa is out of stock.
Leftovers: This gets better on day two; portion it into containers with Earthly Grains couscous or quinoa, or shred the meat off the bones for wraps.
Miso Butter Salmon with Ginger Bok Choy and Edamame
🐟
Miso Butter Salmon with Ginger Bok Choy and Edamame
Weeknight dinner · Japanese · 30 min · 2 servings
♡

Crisp-skinned salmon lacquered in salty-sweet miso butter, with blistered bok choy and buttery edamame soaking up the pan glaze.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
?
Swap: No white miso? Use an extra splash of Soyaki plus a spoon of Friendly Farms Greek yogurt for a similar savory-tangy glaze.
Leftovers: Flake cold salmon over rice with the edamame and a drizzle of Soyaki for a next-day rice bowl; do not microwave it hard or it dries out.

♡

?
?
?
?
?

?
?

?

?

?
?

?
?
?

Yucatecan Sopa de Lima with Crisp Tortilla Strips

?

Alsatian Coq au Riesling with Bacon and Mushrooms
🍷
Alsatian Coq au Riesling with Bacon and Mushrooms

Pounded cutlets pinned with sage and prosciutto that crisps into salty lace, deglazed with white wine and butter, alongside artichokes browned hard in the second pan.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
Swap: No marinated artichokes? Blister a bag of Season's Choice green beans in the same pan with the garlic instead.
Leftovers: Best straight from the pan, but leftover cutlets are excellent cold the next day, sliced over greens with lemon and olive oil.
Seco de Pollo: Ecuadorian Beer-Braised Chicken
🍗
Seco de Pollo: Ecuadorian Beer-Braised Chicken
Big batch cook · Ecuadorian · 75 min · 6 servings
♡

Chicken braised until it slides off the bone in a blended cilantro-and-beer sauce that cooks down from shocking green to deep olive, brightened with lime-pickled red onion.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
Swap: No lager? Use 1 1/2 cups chicken broth plus 1 tbsp Fusia rice vinegar for a similar bright tang.
Leftovers: Refrigerates 4 days and freezes 3 months; the sauce tightens when cold, so reheat covered with a splash of water.
Beef Lok Lak with Tuk Meric
🥩
Beef Lok Lak with Tuk Meric
Weeknight dinner · Cambodian · 30 min · 2 servings
♡

Cubes of steak seared black in spots and glazed sticky, piled on a cold tomato salad under a runny fried egg, with a fiercely sour lime-and-black-pepper dip for every bite.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
Swap: No steak? Cube 1 1/4 lb Aldi pork loin and sear it exactly the same way, just a minute longer per batch.
Leftovers: The beef keeps 3 days; reheat it fast in a screaming skillet and build the salad and dip fresh, since the lime dulls overnight.
Kure na Paprice: Czech Paprika Cream Chicken
🥘
Kure na Paprice: Czech Paprika Cream Chicken
Weeknight dinner · Czech · 40 min · 2 servings
♡

Thighs braised in a brick-red sauce built on a shameless amount of sweet paprika, caraway, and marjoram, then finished with cream and tempered sour cream over buttered noodles.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: No heavy cream? Use 1 cup Friendly Farms whole milk and add an extra tablespoon of flour at the roux step.
Leftovers: Keeps 3 days; reheat over low heat without boiling so the sour cream stays smooth, and cook the noodles fresh.
Tico Casado: Pork Chops with Gallo Pinto
🍛
Tico Casado: Pork Chops with Gallo Pinto
Weeknight dinner · Costa Rican · 40 min · 2 servings
♡

Thick chops lacquered in a tangy, cumin-heavy Lizano-style sauce, plated the Costa Rican way with purple-stained gallo pinto and sticky caramelized plantains.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
Swap: No ripe plantains? Fry thick rounds of sweet potato in the same oil until the edges caramelize.
Leftovers: Gallo pinto is better on day two; reheat it in a skillet with a splash of water and crown it with a fried egg.
Me'orav Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Mixed Grill
🥙
Me'orav Yerushalmi: Jerusalem Mixed Grill
Big batch cook · Israeli · 50 min · 6 servings
♡

Griddle-charred chicken and livers tumbled with frizzled onions and a fistful of cumin, turmeric, and baharat, stuffed into pita with runny tahini and a green streak of zhoug.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: Squeamish about livers? Use another pound of chicken thighs and add an extra teaspoon of baharat for depth.
Leftovers: The meat keeps 4 days and freezes 2 months; reheat it in a dry, ripping-hot skillet to bring the crisp edges back rather than microwaving.
Macanese Minchi with Crispy Potatoes and Fried Eggs
🍳
Macanese Minchi with Crispy Potatoes and Fried Eggs
Weeknight dinner · Macanese · 35 min · 2 servings
♡

Macau's great comfort dish: soy-and-Worcestershire beef tangled with craggy fried potato cubes and crowned with a lacy fried egg.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
?
?
Swap: If the frozen diced potatoes are sold out, cut two russets into small cubes, parboil them for a few minutes, and pat them very dry before frying.
Leftovers: Refrigerate the beef and potatoes together up to three days and reheat in a dry hot skillet so the potato edges crisp back up before you fry a fresh egg.
Sindhi Seyal Murgh, Smothered in Garlic and Cilantro
🌿
Sindhi Seyal Murgh, Smothered in Garlic and Cilantro
Weeknight dinner · Pakistani Sindhi · 40 min · 2 servings
♡

Chicken braised down into a fistful of garlic, split green chilies, and an almost indecent amount of cilantro until the masala clings tight to every piece.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: No fresh green chilies at the store? Use a spoonful of Green Dragon Hot Sauce stirred in with the yogurt for the same grassy heat.
Leftovers: This tastes even better on day two once the garlic mellows; store it up to three days and reheat gently with a splash of water to loosen the masala.
Venetian Shrimp in Saor over Soft Parmesan Polenta
🦐
Venetian Shrimp in Saor over Soft Parmesan Polenta
Weeknight dinner · Venetian · 35 min · 2 servings
♡

Sweet-sour saor onions slumped in vinegar with raisins and pine nuts, spooned over seared red shrimp and a warm pool of parmesan polenta.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: If pine nuts are out of stock, slivered almonds toasted in a dry pan give the same sweet crunch against the vinegar.
Leftovers: The saor shrimp are traditionally eaten cold the next day; keep them chilled up to two days and eat them straight from the fridge on toasted bread.
Honduran Tapado: Garifuna Coconut Chicken and Shrimp Stew
🥥
Honduran Tapado: Garifuna Coconut Chicken and Shrimp Stew
Big batch cook · Honduran · 65 min · 6 servings
♡

A Caribbean-coast pot from Honduras where coconut milk simmers gold with cumin and lime until chicken, plantain, and sweet red shrimp fall together.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: No green plantains in produce? Use a large sweet potato cut into thick chunks and add it with the baby potatoes.
Leftovers: Store up to four days; reheat over low heat only until steaming so the shrimp stay tender, and freeze portions before adding the shrimp if you want them perfect later.
Balinese Sate Lilit Chicken with Sambal Matah
🔥
Balinese Sate Lilit Chicken with Sambal Matah
Weeknight dinner · Balinese · 35 min · 2 servings
♡

Lemongrass and coconut chicken patties charred hard in a skillet, then buried under raw sambal matah that hisses when the hot coconut oil hits it.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: If lemongrass paste is missing, finely mince the pale bottom of two fresh lemongrass stalks, or use the zest of an extra lime plus a little grated ginger.
Leftovers: Keep the patties and sambal in separate containers up to three days; reheat the patties in a skillet and spoon the cold sambal over at the last second.
Austrian Pork Schnitzel with Warm Vinegar Potato Salad
🍋
Austrian Pork Schnitzel with Warm Vinegar Potato Salad
Weeknight dinner · Austrian · 40 min · 2 servings
♡

Shatteringly crisp, puffed golden schnitzel with a hard squeeze of lemon, next to warm Erdapfelsalat slick with mustard, vinegar, and shaved red onion.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
Swap: Thin-cut chicken breasts pounded the same way stand in perfectly, and a spoonful of any berry jam on the side plays the part of lingonberry.
Leftovers: The potato salad keeps three days and only gets better; re-crisp leftover schnitzel in a hot dry skillet or oven rather than the microwave.
Tunisian Ojja with Merguez and Eggs
🌶️
Tunisian Ojja with Merguez and Eggs
Weeknight dinner · Tunisian · 35 min · 2 servings
♡

Tunis in a skillet: harissa and crushed caraway fried into tomatoes and peppers with spicy merguez, with eggs poached right in the fiery sauce.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
Swap: No merguez on the counter? Use Never Any! spicy sausage and add an extra spoonful of harissa plus a pinch more caraway to get the same North African punch.
Leftovers: The sauce alone keeps four days and freezes well; reheat it in a skillet and poach fresh eggs in it rather than saving the cooked ones.
Bahamian Brown Stew Chicken with Thyme and Hot Pepper
🍗
Bahamian Brown Stew Chicken with Thyme and Hot Pepper
Big batch cook · Bahamian · 75 min · 6 servings
♡

Nassau-style stew chicken, where sugar burnt almost to bitterness lacquers the meat mahogany before it simmers soft with thyme, allspice, and hot sauce.

Ingredients — tap to check off
?
?
?
Swap: If bone-in pieces are picked over, boneless thighs work; brown them the same way and cut the covered simmer roughly in half.
Leftovers: This deepens overnight and keeps four days; pull the meat off the bones and reheat it in the gravy, or freeze it in portions for up to three months.

🍚 Gochujang Bulgogi Beef Bowls with Chili Onion Crunch
Step 1 of 7

Heat a large skillet over medium-high until a flicked drop of water skitters and evaporates. Add the ground beef, press it into one flat slab, and leave it completely alone so it can brown.

💡Do not stir yet
Step 2 of 7

While the beef browns, toss the cucumber coins with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt, and set them aside to quick-pickle.

Step 3 of 7

Break the beef into craggy bite-size pieces, then add the garlic and scallion whites. Stir constantly until the garlic smells sweet rather than raw.

Step 4 of 7

Pour in the Gochujang Sauce and soy sauce and drop the heat to medium. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the meat instead of pooling.

💡Glossy, not soupy
Step 5 of 7

Microwave the frozen jasmine rice according to the bag while the beef glazes, then fluff it with a fork.

Step 6 of 7

In a small nonstick pan over medium heat, fry the eggs in a slick of olive oil until the whites are fully set and the edges go lacy and brown but the yolks still jiggle.

Step 7 of 7

Build each bowl with rice, the glazed beef, a fried egg, and the pickled cucumber. Finish with the chili onion crunch, a drizzle of sesame oil, and the sliced scallion greens.

🌮 Carne Asada Tacos with Charred Peppers and Chili Lime Crema
Step 1 of 8

Pull the carne asada out of the fridge, blot it very dry with paper towels, and let it sit on the counter while you prep everything else.

💡Dry, room-temp meat sears instead of steams
Step 2 of 8

Stir the sour cream with the Chili Lime Seasoning and a squeeze of lime, thinning with a splash of water until it drizzles off the spoon. Chop the onion and cilantro while you are at it.

Step 3 of 8

Set a cast iron skillet over high heat until it just begins to wisp smoke. Lay the steak in a single uncrowded layer and do not move it until a dark brown crust forms.

💡Work in two batches if needed
Step 4 of 8

Flip the steak and cook the second side until browned and the thin edges look crisp and lacquered. Move it to a cutting board to rest.

Step 5 of 8

Dump the frozen peppers and onions straight into the same screaming-hot pan and spread them out. Leave them undisturbed so the liquid cooks off and the edges char in the beef fat.

Step 6 of 8

Warm the tortillas in a second dry skillet over medium-high, or directly over a gas flame, until they are pliable and freckled with black spots.

Step 7 of 8

Slice the rested steak against the grain into thin strips; the juices should stay on the board, not run out.

Step 8 of 8

Stack two tortillas per taco and load with steak, charred peppers, salsa verde, cheese, onion, and cilantro, then drizzle the chili lime crema over the top.

🍤 Thai Red Curry Shrimp with Blistered Green Beans
Step 1 of 7

Spread the thawed shrimp on paper towels and press them dry, then season lightly with salt. Wet shrimp will never take on color.

Step 2 of 7

Heat a wide skillet over high with a slick of olive oil until it shimmers. Add the green beans straight from the freezer and let them sit until the undersides are blistered and browned in spots.

Step 3 of 7

Push the beans to one side, add the bell pepper, and stir just until the slices soften at the edges but still snap. Scrape everything onto a plate.

Step 4 of 7

Lower the heat to medium and pour in the Thai Red Curry Sauce and coconut milk. Simmer until the surface shines with a thin ring of orange oil.

💡That oil ring means the curry has bloomed
Step 5 of 7

Slide the shrimp into the curry in one layer and poach gently, turning once, until they curl into loose C shapes and turn opaque. Heat the rice pouches while they cook.

💡Tight O shapes mean overcooked
Step 6 of 7

Return the vegetables to the pan and stir in the fish sauce, brown sugar, and a big squeeze of lime. Taste and add more lime until it tastes bright rather than flat.

Step 7 of 7

Spoon over the jasmine rice and shower with torn Thai basil, with the second lime half on the side.

🍲 Harissa Chicken and Chickpea Tagine with Apricots
Step 1 of 9

Pat the chicken thighs bone dry and season all over with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high with a thin film of olive oil until it shimmers.

Step 2 of 9

Lay the thighs in skin side down without crowding and leave them untouched until the skin is deep golden and releases from the pot on its own.

💡If it sticks, it is not ready to flip
Step 3 of 9

Flip and brown the second side briefly, then move the thighs to a plate. Pour off all but a couple of tablespoons of the rendered fat.

Step 4 of 9

Add the onion to the pot with a pinch of salt and cook over medium, scraping up the browned bits, until softened and translucent at the edges.

Step 5 of 9

Stir in the garlic, cumin, cinnamon, and Harissa and cook until the paste darkens a shade and smells toasty rather than raw.

💡Blooming the spices in fat is what makes this taste layered
Step 6 of 9

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth, then add the chickpeas and apricots. Nestle the chicken back in skin side up so the tops stay above the liquid.

Step 7 of 9

Bring to a bare simmer, cover partially, and cook over low until the chicken is falling off the bone and the sauce has reduced and darkened. Stir once halfway through to keep the bottom from catching.

Step 8 of 9

Uncover and simmer hard for the last stretch to concentrate the sauce, then taste for salt. It should be sweet, smoky, and a little fiery.

Step 9 of 9

Serve in bowls with a big spoonful of Greek yogurt swirled in and a handful of chopped herbs over the top.

🐟 Miso Butter Salmon with Ginger Bok Choy and Edamame
Step 1 of 8

Whisk the miso, Soyaki, and rice vinegar into a smooth glaze. Pat the salmon completely dry and season the flesh side lightly with salt.

💡Miso burns fast, so it goes on late
Step 2 of 8

Heat a nonstick or cast iron skillet over medium with a little olive oil. Lay the salmon in skin side down and press each fillet flat with a spatula for the first few seconds so the skin makes full contact.

Step 3 of 8

Cook without moving the fillets until the skin is crisp and the flesh has turned opaque and pale most of the way up the sides.

💡Watch the color creep up the side of the fillet
Step 4 of 8

Flip the salmon, brush the glaze generously over the crisp skin and sides, and cook just until the center is barely translucent when you peek with a fork.

Step 5 of 8

Move the salmon to plates and let it rest while you cook the vegetables; carryover heat finishes the middle.

Step 6 of 8

Raise the heat to medium-high, add the butter and ginger to the same pan, and lay the bok choy in cut side down. Sear until the cut faces are browned and the stems are crisp-tender.

Step 7 of 8

Toss in the frozen edamame and any leftover glaze, and stir until the beans are hot and coated in the ginger butter. Heat the rice pouch while this finishes.

Step 8 of 8

Plate the salmon over rice with the bok choy and edamame alongside, and shower everything with Everything But The Bagel seasoning.

🍋 Lemon Oregano Chicken Souvlaki with Whipped Feta
Step 1 of 8

Toss the chicken cubes with the lemon zest, half the garlic, the oregano, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Let it sit on the counter while you make the whipped feta.

Step 2 of 8

Blitz the feta, Greek yogurt, remaining garlic, and a squeeze of lemon in a food processor until it is completely smooth and spreadable, scraping the sides once.

💡Add a splash of the artichoke oil if it stalls
Step 3 of 8

Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high until a drop of water dances. Add the chicken in a single layer with space between the pieces and leave it undisturbed to build a crust.

💡Crowding the pan gives you gray chicken
Step 4 of 8

Toss the chicken and continue cooking until the cubes are browned on multiple sides and firm to the touch with no pink at the center.

Step 5 of 8

Move the chicken to a plate, add the cherry tomatoes to the hot pan, and let them sit until the skins blister and a few burst. Squeeze in the rest of the lemon and scrape up the browned bits.

Step 6 of 8

Warm the naan directly in a dry skillet or over a gas flame until it puffs slightly and picks up a few dark spots.

Step 7 of 8

Smear a thick layer of whipped feta across each naan, then pile on the chicken, blistered tomatoes, drained artichokes, and olives.

Step 8 of 8

Finish with chopped dill, a crack of black pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil.

🍜 Caramelized Lemongrass Pork Noodle Bowls
Step 1 of 8

Bring a pot of water to a boil for the noodles. While it heats, toss the carrot with the juice of half a lime and a pinch of salt to quick-pickle.

Step 2 of 8

Whisk the Sweet Chili Sauce, sriracha, 1 tbsp of the fish sauce, and the juice of one lime into a pourable dressing. Taste and adjust until it is equal parts sweet, salty, and sour.

Step 3 of 8

Cook the rice noodles just until tender, then drain and rinse under cold water until they are completely cool and no longer sticky.

💡Cold rinsing stops the noodles from clumping
Step 4 of 8

Heat a skillet over medium-high until very hot. Add the pork in one flat layer and leave it alone until the underside is browned and crusty.

Step 5 of 8

Break the pork into pieces, add the lemongrass, and stir until it smells sharply citrusy.

Step 6 of 8

Sprinkle in the brown sugar and the remaining 2 tbsp fish sauce and cook, stirring often, until the liquid reduces to a dark syrup that lacquers the meat and the edges go crisp.

💡Watch closely, the sugar goes from caramel to burnt quickly
Step 7 of 8

Divide the noodles between two deep bowls and top with the caramelized pork, pickled carrot, cucumber ribbons, and a generous handful of mint and cilantro.

Step 8 of 8

Pour the dressing over each bowl, scatter the crushed peanuts, and toss everything together at the table with the last lime half on the side.

🥘 Andouille, Chicken and Shrimp Jambalaya
Step 1 of 9

Heat a wide heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium with a little olive oil. Add the sausage coins in one layer and cook until the edges curl and brown and orange fat pools in the pot.

💡That rendered fat is the flavor base
Step 2 of 9

Scoop the sausage out with a slotted spoon. Season the chicken chunks with half the Cajun seasoning, then brown them in the sausage fat over medium-high without stirring for the first few minutes.

Step 3 of 9

Remove the chicken and add the onion, bell pepper, and celery with a pinch of salt. Cook over medium, scraping the browned crust off the bottom, until the vegetables slump and the onion turns translucent.

Step 4 of 9

Stir in the garlic and remaining Cajun seasoning and cook until the pot smells intensely spiced and the paste darkens slightly.

Step 5 of 9

Add the rice and stir constantly so every grain gets coated in the seasoned fat and turns slightly translucent at the edges.

💡Toasting the rice keeps the grains separate
Step 6 of 9

Pour in the broth and diced tomatoes with their juice, return the sausage and chicken along with any collected juices, and bring to a full boil.

Step 7 of 9

Drop the heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook without lifting the lid or stirring until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

💡Peeking lets out the steam the rice needs
Step 8 of 9

Scatter the shrimp over the surface, replace the lid, and let them steam off the heat until they are pink, opaque, and curled.

Step 9 of 9

Fluff everything together with a fork, taste for salt, and finish with a thick layer of sliced scallions.

🍛 Broiler-Charred Tikka Masala Thighs
Step 1 of 7

Set an oven rack about 6 inches under the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Line a sheet pan with foil so the sugars in the yogurt don't weld themselves to the metal.

💡Foil now saves scrubbing later.
Step 2 of 7

Toss the thighs with the Greek yogurt, half the garlic, all the ginger, 2 teaspoons of the garam masala, and a big pinch of salt until every piece is slicked. Spread them out on the pan with space between them.

💡Crowding steams instead of chars.
Step 3 of 7

Broil until the tops are blistered with real black spots and the edges look dry and pulled-in, about 10 minutes. Don't flip them.

💡You want char, not just color.
Step 4 of 7

While the chicken broils, melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and add the remaining garlic and the last teaspoon of garam masala. Stir constantly for about a minute until the spice smells toasty and darkens slightly.

💡Blooming spice in fat is the whole trick.
Step 5 of 7

Pour in the simmer sauce, scrape the pan bottom, and let it bubble gently until it thickens enough to coat a spoon, about 5 minutes.

Step 6 of 7

Cut the charred chicken into bite-size chunks, add it plus any juices from the foil to the sauce, and simmer 4 minutes so the meat drinks up the sauce.

💡Those pan juices are pure flavor.
Step 7 of 7

Warm the naan in a dry skillet over medium-high for about a minute per side until it puffs and freckles. Finish the curry with a squeeze of lemon and a shower of cilantro.

💡Acid at the end wakes everything up.
🥩 Lomo Saltado with Crispy Fries
Step 1 of 8

Heat the oven to 425F, spread the fries in a single layer on a sheet pan, and bake until deep golden and rigid, about 20 minutes. They need to be genuinely crisp because they go into a wet pan at the end.

💡Soggy fries ruin the dish.
Step 2 of 8

While the fries bake, whisk the soy sauce, red wine vinegar, cumin, and Green Dragon together in a small bowl and set it right next to the stove. The stir-fry moves fast once it starts.

💡Mise en place is mandatory here.
Step 3 of 8

Pat the steak strips very dry with paper towels and season with pepper. Heat a cast iron or heavy skillet over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until a drop of water evaporates on contact and the pan just begins to shimmer.

💡Dry meat plus screaming pan equals crust.
Step 4 of 8

Add a slick of oil and lay the steak in one layer. Sear undisturbed for 2 minutes until the underside is deeply browned, toss for 20 seconds more, then pull it onto a plate.

💡Undercook slightly; it returns to the pan.
Step 5 of 8

Drop the onion wedges into the same pan over high heat and let them char for 3 minutes, tossing only once, until the edges are blackened but the layers still have snap.

Step 6 of 8

Add the garlic and tomato wedges and cook 1 minute, just until the tomatoes soften at the edges but hold their shape.

💡Tomatoes should slump, not collapse.
Step 7 of 8

Return the steak and any resting juices, pour in the sauce, and toss for 1 minute until it reduces to a glossy coating.

Step 8 of 8

Microwave the rice pouch, then kill the heat and fold the hot fries into the skillet so they catch the sauce without going limp. Scatter cilantro and serve immediately over rice.

💡Serve the second it's tossed.
🌶️ Chili Crunch Mapo Beef and Tofu
Step 1 of 7

Cube the tofu and let it drain on a towel while you cook. In a small cup, stir the cornstarch into 1/2 cup cold water until no lumps remain and set it aside.

💡Drier tofu holds together better.
Step 2 of 7

Heat a wok or wide skillet over medium-high and brown the beef, pressing it flat and leaving it alone so it forms a crust, about 5 minutes total. You want crisp browned bits, not gray crumbles.

💡Resist stirring for the first 2 minutes.
Step 3 of 7

Push the beef to one side, add the garlic, ginger, and Crunchy Chili Onion to the bare spot, and stir for 1 minute until the chili oil turns brilliant red and smells fragrant.

💡Blooming the chili oil deepens the color.
Step 4 of 7

Pour in the soy sauce, sriracha, umami seasoning, and 1 cup water, then simmer 3 minutes to pull it together into a loose sauce.

Step 5 of 7

Slide the tofu in and simmer gently for 5 minutes without stirring, nudging the pan side to side instead so the cubes stay whole.

💡Shake the pan, never the spoon.
Step 6 of 7

Stir the cornstarch slurry again and pour it in, then let it bubble for about a minute until the sauce turns glossy and thickly coats the back of a spoon.

💡Re-stir the slurry; it settles fast.
Step 7 of 7

Microwave the jasmine rice according to the bag while the sauce thickens, then spoon the mapo over the rice and blanket it with scallions.

🥘 Big-Batch Spanish Chorizo and Chicken Rice
Step 1 of 8

Season the thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat a film of olive oil in a wide Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high until it shimmers, then sear the chicken in batches, 5 minutes on the first side without moving it, until a mahogany crust forms.

💡Batches, not a crowded pile.
Step 2 of 8

Flip for 2 minutes, then move the chicken to a plate. It will finish cooking in the rice, so don't chase doneness now.

Step 3 of 8

Drop the chorizo coins into the same pot over medium heat and render for 3 minutes until the edges curl and the fat runs bright orange.

💡That orange fat is your flavor base.
Step 4 of 8

Add the garlic and the frozen peppers and onions and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until all the released water has boiled off and the vegetables start to sizzle again.

💡Wait for the sizzle to return.
Step 5 of 8

Stir in the smoked paprika and turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the diced tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until the mixture darkens and pulls away from the pan bottom.

💡Don't let the paprika scorch.
Step 6 of 8

Add the rice and stir for a minute so every grain is coated in the fat, then pour in the broth, scatter in the chickpeas, and nestle the chicken and its juices on top. Bring to a full boil.

Step 7 of 8

Reduce to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 20 minutes completely undisturbed. Lifting the lid lets out the steam the rice needs.

💡No peeking.
Step 8 of 8

Scatter the frozen peas over the top, replace the lid, pull the pot off the heat, and rest 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork, shred the chicken slightly into the rice, and serve with lemon wedges.

💡The rest sets the grains.
🍗 Sticky Filipino Chicken Adobo
Step 1 of 7

Pat the thighs bone dry and season with pepper only, since the soy brings plenty of salt. Lay them skin down in a cold skillet, set it over medium-high, and let the fat render and the skin go deep golden and crackly, about 8 minutes.

💡Starting cold renders more fat.
Step 2 of 7

Flip and sear the underside for 2 minutes, then move the chicken to a plate and pour off all but about a tablespoon of the fat.

Step 3 of 7

Add the smashed garlic to the reserved fat and stir for 1 minute until it turns pale gold and perfumed. Pull it back from the heat if it starts browning fast.

💡Burnt garlic turns the whole braise bitter.
Step 4 of 7

Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, bay leaves, cracked peppercorns, brown sugar, and 1/2 cup water. Boil hard and uncovered for 3 minutes without stirring, which cooks off the raw bite of the vinegar.

💡Do not stir during this boil.
Step 5 of 7

Return the chicken skin side up so the skin stays above the liquid, lower the heat to a bare simmer, and cook 20 minutes until the meat pulls easily from the bone.

💡Skin above the waterline stays crisp.
Step 6 of 7

Lift the chicken out, raise the heat, and reduce the sauce for 5 minutes until it is syrupy and coats the back of a spoon in a dark sheet.

Step 7 of 7

Heat the jasmine rice while the sauce reduces, then spoon the glaze over the chicken and rice and finish with scallions.

💡Sauce the rice generously.
🧆 Turkish Kofte with Harissa Butter and Garlic Yogurt
Step 1 of 8

Grate the onion, then squeeze it hard in a paper towel over the sink until it stops dripping. Wet onion will steam the kofte instead of letting them brown.

💡Squeeze it drier than you think.
Step 2 of 8

Knead the beef with the squeezed onion, cumin, one grated garlic clove, salt, and pepper for a full minute until the mixture turns tacky and holds together like paste.

💡Tacky mix means kofte that don't fall apart.
Step 3 of 8

Shape into 6 flat oblong logs about an inch thick and set them on a plate in the fridge while the pan heats.

Step 4 of 8

Stir the remaining grated garlic into the yogurt with a squeeze of lemon and a good pinch of salt, then spread it in a thick swoosh across two plates.

Step 5 of 8

Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high for 3 minutes until a flicked drop of water skitters and evaporates instantly.

💡A properly hot pan is non-negotiable.
Step 6 of 8

Add a little oil and sear the kofte undisturbed for 4 minutes until the underside is mahogany and releases from the pan on its own.

💡If it sticks, it isn't ready to flip.
Step 7 of 8

Flip and cook 3 minutes more until the centers feel firm and springy rather than squishy. Meanwhile toss the tomatoes, cucumber, and parsley with lemon juice, olive oil, and salt.

Step 8 of 8

Melt the butter with the harissa in a small pan over medium for 1 minute until it foams and stains red, then pile the kofte on the yogurt, pour the butter over, and serve with the salad and warm flatbread.

💡Pour it while it's still sizzling.
🍤 Jerk Shrimp with Coconut Rice and Beans
Step 1 of 8

Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then combine it in a saucepan with the coconut milk, 1/2 cup water, one smashed garlic clove, and a good pinch of salt. Bring to a boil over high heat.

💡Rinsing keeps the rice from going gluey.
Step 2 of 8

Cover, drop to the lowest heat, and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the liquid is absorbed and small craters appear on the surface.

Step 3 of 8

While it cooks, mash the jerk paste together: allspice, thyme, brown sugar, soy sauce, hot sauce, minced scallion whites, the remaining 2 cloves of garlic minced, and the juice of one lime.

Step 4 of 8

Toss the shrimp with about two-thirds of the paste and let them sit 10 minutes at room temperature. Any longer and the lime starts to firm up the texture.

💡Ten minutes is the sweet spot.
Step 5 of 8

Fork the kidney beans into the finished rice, replace the lid, and let it sit off the heat for 5 minutes to warm the beans through.

Step 6 of 8

Heat a heavy skillet over high for 2 minutes until it smokes faintly, then add a slick of oil.

💡Jerk needs real char to taste right.
Step 7 of 8

Lay the shrimp in a single layer and sear 2 minutes without moving them, until the undersides are caramelized dark, then flip for 1 minute until they curl into loose Cs and turn opaque.

💡A tight O means overcooked.
Step 8 of 8

Add the remaining paste with a splash of water and toss 30 seconds to glaze. Serve over the coconut rice with scallion greens and wedges from the second lime.

🍝 Big-Batch Vodka Sauce Baked Ziti with Sausage
Step 1 of 9

Heat the oven to 400F and put a large pot of well-salted water on to boil. Salt it until it tastes like a mild broth.

Step 2 of 9

Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it into rough chunks and then leaving it alone so it develops crust, about 8 minutes. Chase browned bits, not uniform crumbles.

💡Big craggy pieces beat fine crumbles.
Step 3 of 9

Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and stir for 1 minute until fragrant and the fat turns rosy.

Step 4 of 9

Pour in both jars of vodka sauce, scrape up every browned bit from the pan bottom, and simmer gently for 10 minutes until it thickens and deepens in color.

💡The fond is where the flavor lives.
Step 5 of 9

Meanwhile boil the pasta about 2 minutes shy of the package's al dente, so it still has a firm chalky center. Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain.

💡It finishes cooking in the oven.
Step 6 of 9

While the pasta cooks, stir the ricotta with the egg, parmesan, and a big pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.

💡The egg keeps the ricotta from weeping.
Step 7 of 9

Toss the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of pasta water until everything is coated and glossy. Spread half in a 9x13 dish, dollop over the ricotta mixture and the pesto, then add the remaining pasta and blanket with mozzarella.

💡Leave the ricotta in pockets, don't stir it in.
Step 8 of 9

Bake uncovered for 20 minutes until the cheese is browned in patches and the sauce bubbles up the sides of the dish.

Step 9 of 9

Rest 10 minutes before cutting so the layers set instead of sliding, then tear basil over the top.

💡Cutting too soon makes soup.
🥙 Zhoug Chicken Shawarma Bowls
Step 1 of 7

Set a cast iron or heavy stainless skillet over medium-high and let it preheat dry for a full 2 minutes, until a flicked drop of water skitters instead of sitting still. Pat the thighs dry with paper towels while it heats.

💡A wet thigh steams; a dry one chars.
Step 2 of 7

Add a slick of olive oil, then lay the thighs down in a single layer with space between them. Sear undisturbed until the underside is deep mahogany and the edges have crisped, about 5 minutes.

💡Crowding the pan kills the crust.
Step 3 of 7

Flip and cook another 5 minutes, until the thickest part is opaque all the way through and the juices run clear. While it cooks, dice the cucumber and tomatoes.

Step 4 of 7

Toss the cucumber, tomato, red onion, and parsley with the juice of half the lemon, a glug of olive oil, salt, and plenty of black pepper. Taste it — it should be aggressively lemony.

Step 5 of 7

Stir the zhoug into the Greek yogurt with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of the remaining lemon until it turns pale green and pourable.

💡Thin with a splash of water if it's too stiff to drizzle.
Step 6 of 7

Move the chicken to a cutting board and rest it for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain into thick strips. Meanwhile, blister the naan directly in the hot skillet, about 1 minute per side.

💡Resting keeps the juices in the meat.
Step 7 of 7

Smear hummus across the bottom of two shallow bowls, then heap on the salad and the sliced chicken. Drizzle the zhoug yogurt over everything and dust with sumac.

🍤 Bahian Shrimp Moqueca
Step 1 of 7

Toss the shrimp with the juice of one lime, a big pinch of salt, and black pepper. Let them sit while you build the base.

💡A quick lime cure firms up the shrimp.
Step 2 of 7

Warm 2 tablespoons olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat, then add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook until soft, floppy, and translucent at the edges, about 5 minutes.

Step 3 of 7

Add the garlic, paprika, and tomato paste and stir constantly for 1 minute, until the paste darkens to brick red and the pan smells toasty rather than raw.

💡Raw tomato paste tastes tinny — cook it out.
Step 4 of 7

Pour in the coconut milk and the frozen peppers and onions, scraping the bottom of the pan. Simmer over medium-low for 10 minutes, until the broth thickens slightly and orange fat pools at the edges.

💡Heat the rice while this reduces.
Step 5 of 7

Slide the shrimp into the broth in a single layer and poach gently for 3 minutes, spooning liquid over the tops, until they turn opaque and curl into loose C shapes.

💡Tight O shapes mean they went too far.
Step 6 of 7

Kill the heat and stir in most of the cilantro, the Chili Lime Seasoning, and the juice of the second lime. Taste and add salt until the coconut sweetness snaps into focus.

Step 7 of 7

Spoon the moqueca over hot jasmine rice in wide bowls and finish with the remaining cilantro and a lime wedge.

🍜 Mamak-Style Mee Goreng with Shrimp and Egg
Step 1 of 7

Boil the noodles one minute shy of the package time so they still have spring, then drain, rinse under cold water, and toss with a teaspoon of oil so they don't fuse.

💡Undercook them — they finish in the pan.
Step 2 of 7

Whisk the sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, ketchup, and sriracha together in a small bowl. This is your gravy, and having it premixed is the whole trick to a fast stir-fry.

Step 3 of 7

Heat your largest skillet over high until a bead of oil shimmers and just barely wisps smoke. Pour in the eggs and scramble hard for 1 minute into big soft curds, then scrape them onto a plate.

Step 4 of 7

Add another splash of oil and lay the shrimp down in one layer. Sear about 1 minute per side, until pink and opaque at the edges, then move them to the plate with the eggs.

💡They will finish cooking when everything comes back together.
Step 5 of 7

Toss in the garlic and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the cabbage wilts at the edges but the ribs still crunch.

Step 6 of 7

Add the drained noodles and all of the gravy, then toss with tongs for 2 minutes, letting the noodles sit still for a few seconds at a time so they catch color against the hot metal.

💡Stillness is where the smoky wok flavor comes from.
Step 7 of 7

Fold the shrimp, egg, and scallions back in and turn off the heat. Squeeze the lime over the top and finish with spoonfuls of Crunchy Chili Onion.

🥘 Persian Lemon-Turmeric Chicken and Chickpea Khoresh
Step 1 of 8

Pat the thighs very dry and season them hard with salt and pepper on both sides. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until it shimmers and thins out.

Step 2 of 8

Brown the chicken in two batches, about 4 minutes per side, until the surface is deep gold and the pieces release from the pot without sticking.

💡If a thigh grips the pan, it isn't browned yet.
Step 3 of 8

Move the chicken to a plate and add the onions with a big pinch of salt. Cook over medium for 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping up the browned bits, until they collapse into a deep gold jam.

💡Juice the lemons and drain the chickpeas while this happens.
Step 4 of 8

Stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, until the whole pot smells toasted and the paste turns brick colored.

Step 5 of 8

Return the chicken and any juices, then add the broth and chickpeas. Bring to a bare simmer, cover, and cook for 30 minutes, until the meat pulls away from the bone under gentle fork pressure.

💡Bubbles should barely break the surface.
Step 6 of 8

Uncover, stir in the lemon juice and cranberries, and simmer 10 minutes more so the liquid tightens around the chickpeas and the cranberries plump.

Step 7 of 8

Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks and fish out the bones. Taste and push it further with salt and more lemon until it tastes bright, not muddy.

💡Persian stews should land sour first, rich second.
Step 8 of 8

Heat the basmati and serve the khoresh ladled over it, showered with parsley and finished with a cold spoonful of yogurt.

🥩 Skirt Steak with Hand-Chopped Chimichurri
Step 1 of 9

Heat the oven to 450°F and salt the steak generously on both sides, then leave it on the counter to take the chill off while everything else comes together.

💡Salt early so it has time to penetrate.
Step 2 of 9

Toss the halved potatoes with olive oil and salt, spread them cut-side down on a sheet pan, and roast for 20 minutes until the cut faces are crisp and deep gold.

💡Cut-side down is what builds the crust.
Step 3 of 9

While they roast, finely chop the parsley, garlic, and shallot by hand and stir them together with the vinegar, oregano, pepper flakes, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 cup olive oil.

💡A blender turns chimichurri into sad green paste.
Step 4 of 9

Let the chimichurri sit for 10 minutes so the garlic mellows and the oregano rehydrates. Taste it — it should be sharp enough to make you blink.

Step 5 of 9

Set a cast iron skillet over high heat for 4 minutes, until it is faintly smoking and the surface looks dull rather than shiny.

Step 6 of 9

Pat the steak bone dry, oil it lightly, and lay it down. Sear for 3 minutes without touching it at all, until a dark, continuous crust forms.

💡Every peek costs you crust.
Step 7 of 9

Flip and sear 3 minutes more for medium-rare — the center should feel like the fleshy pad below your thumb when pressed.

Step 8 of 9

Rest the steak on a board for 8 minutes, then find the direction of the muscle fibers and slice thin straight across them.

💡Cutting with the grain makes skirt steak chewy.
Step 9 of 9

Dress the arugula with lemon, olive oil, and salt. Plate the steak, spoon chimichurri over it generously, and add the potatoes with the chimichurri hot sauce alongside.

🥡 Crispy General Tso's Chicken and Broccoli
Step 1 of 8

Toss the chicken cubes with the egg white and 1/2 teaspoon salt, then add the cornstarch and toss again until every piece looks chalky and dry with no wet patches left.

💡The dry cornstarch shell is what shatters.
Step 2 of 8

Pour 1/2 inch of neutral oil into a skillet and heat over medium-high for about 4 minutes, until a dropped scrap of coating sizzles vigorously on contact.

Step 3 of 8

Fry the chicken in two batches for about 4 minutes each, turning once, until pale gold and firm to the touch. Drain on a rack, not paper, so the bottoms stay crisp.

💡Two batches keeps the oil hot enough to crisp.
Step 4 of 8

While the second batch fries, steam or microwave the broccoli for 3 minutes until it turns vivid green and a fork meets slight resistance.

Step 5 of 8

Pour off all but a tablespoon of oil, drop the heat to medium, and add the garlic, ginger, and chiles. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant and just barely blond — never browned.

💡Burnt garlic will ruin the whole sauce.
Step 6 of 8

Pour in the General Tso's sauce and soy sauce and let it bubble for 2 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.

Step 7 of 8

Kill the heat, add the chicken and broccoli, and toss fast for about 30 seconds so everything is glazed but the crust hasn't had time to go soggy.

💡Sauce it at the last possible second.
Step 8 of 8

Heat the jasmine rice and serve immediately, scattered with scallions and sesame seeds.

🍗 Doro Wat-Style Chicken with Jammy Eggs
Step 1 of 8

Put the diced red onions in a wide skillet over medium heat with no fat at all and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until they release their water, collapse, and turn sticky.

💡The dry start is what makes doro wat taste like doro wat.
Step 2 of 8

Meanwhile, lower the eggs into boiling water and cook exactly 7 minutes for jammy centers, then shock them in ice water and peel.

Step 3 of 8

Add the butter to the onions and let it foam, then stir in the harissa, paprika, cardamom, ginger, and garlic. Cook 2 minutes until the mixture darkens to a glossy brick paste.

Step 4 of 8

Cut the chicken into large chunks, season with salt, and fold it into the paste until every piece is coated red.

Step 5 of 8

Pour in the broth, bring to a low simmer, and cook partly covered for 20 minutes, until the chicken shreds under a fork and the sauce has reduced to something that clings rather than pools.

💡Stir once or twice so the bottom doesn't catch.
Step 6 of 8

Score the peeled eggs lightly all over with a knife tip and nestle them into the sauce, spooning it over the tops. Simmer 3 minutes to warm them through.

💡Scoring lets the sauce soak into the whites.
Step 7 of 8

Finish with a squeeze of lemon and salt to taste, then warm the naan in a dry pan for about 1 minute per side until it puffs and spots.

Step 8 of 8

Serve straight from the skillet with torn naan as the scoop — this is a dish meant to be eaten with your hands.

🌶️ Tex-Mex Beef and Black Bean Chili with Unexpected Cheddar
Step 1 of 8

Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high for 2 minutes, then add half the beef and press it into a flat slab. Leave it completely undisturbed for 4 minutes so a genuine brown crust forms.

💡Crowded beef steams gray and tastes like nothing.
Step 2 of 8

Break the slab into chunks and cook 3 more minutes until no pink remains, then move it to a bowl with its juices and repeat with the second half.

Step 3 of 8

Add the onion and bell pepper to the rendered fat and cook over medium for 8 minutes, until softened with browned edges. Drain and rinse the beans while you wait.

Step 4 of 8

Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, and tomato paste and keep it moving for 2 minutes, until the spices smell toasted and the paste darkens against the pot.

💡Blooming the spices in fat doubles their punch.
Step 5 of 8

Return all the beef, then add the salsa, crushed tomatoes, black beans, broth, and a teaspoon of salt. Scrape every browned bit off the bottom as it comes up to heat.

Step 6 of 8

Bring to a simmer, drop to low, and cook uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a trail that closes slowly.

💡If it thickens too fast, add broth a splash at a time.
Step 7 of 8

Taste and correct: more salt if it tastes flat, more chili powder if it tastes sweet, a pinch more cumin if it tastes thin.

Step 8 of 8

Pull it off the heat and let it rest 10 minutes to set up, then ladle into bowls and bury each one under a mound of grated Unexpected Cheddar.

💡Grate the cheddar cold — it crumbles rather than smears.
🔥 Nashville Hot Honey Chicken Thighs
Step 1 of 7

Halve the thighs into rough 3-inch pieces, season them hard with salt and pepper, then toss with the buttermilk in a bowl until every piece is coated. Let them sit while you set up the dredge.

💡Even a short soak seasons the meat through.
Step 2 of 7

Whisk the flour with 1 tsp of the cayenne, 1 tsp of the smoked paprika, the garlic powder, and a big pinch of salt in a shallow dish. Drizzle in 2 tbsp of the buttermilk from the bowl and rake it with a fork so the flour turns shaggy and pebbly.

💡Those flour clumps become the crunchy bits.
Step 3 of 7

Heat the oil in a 10-inch cast iron or heavy skillet over medium-high until it reaches about 350F, or until a pinch of flour sizzles briskly on contact. Press each thigh piece firmly into the dredge on both sides, then lay it in the oil away from you.

💡Crowding drops the oil temperature fast.
Step 4 of 7

Fry in two batches without moving the chicken until the underside is deep mahogany and releases on its own, then flip and fry the second side until the crust is crisp and the thickest piece hits 175F.

💡Adjust heat to keep a steady, lively sizzle.
Step 5 of 7

Move the fried chicken to a rack set over a plate so the bottom crust stays crisp. Carefully spoon 3 tbsp of the hot frying oil into a heatproof bowl and discard the rest.

💡Frying oil is the flavor base for the paste.
Step 6 of 7

Whisk the remaining cayenne and smoked paprika, the brown sugar, and the hot honey into that reserved hot oil until it turns glossy and brick red. Taste it on a pickle and add more cayenne if you want it truly hot.

💡The heat of the oil blooms the spices.
Step 7 of 7

Brush the paste generously over both sides of the chicken and let it soak in while you lay the bread on two plates. Pile the chicken on the bread, top with pickle chips, and drizzle any paste left in the bowl over the top.

💡The bread is a sponge, not a side.
🍤 Sambal Balado Shrimp with Coconut Jasmine Rice
Step 1 of 7

Stir the soy sauce and brown sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves into a syrupy kecap manis. Set it next to the stove along with the chili onion crunch.

💡Have everything at arm's reach; this cooks fast.
Step 2 of 7

Microwave the jasmine rice packets according to the package, then tip the hot rice into a bowl and fold in the coconut milk and a big pinch of salt. Cover and leave it alone so the rice drinks the coconut milk.

💡It should look creamy, not soupy.
Step 3 of 7

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high until it shimmers, then add the shallots and bell pepper. Stir-fry until the shallot edges are browned and the peppers are blistered but still snappy.

💡High heat, constant motion.
Step 4 of 7

Push the vegetables to one side, add the garlic to the bare spot, and stir it in the oil until fragrant and just turning pale gold. Do not let it go past blond or the whole pan turns bitter.

💡Garlic burns in seconds at this heat.
Step 5 of 7

Season the shrimp with salt, spread them in a single layer, and leave them undisturbed until the bottoms turn opaque orange. Flip once and cook until they curl into loose Cs.

💡Tight O-shaped shrimp are overcooked.
Step 6 of 7

Pour in the kecap manis mixture and the chili onion crunch, then toss hard for 30 seconds until the sauce reduces to a glaze that coats every shrimp and slides off the spoon slowly.

💡Kill the heat the moment it turns glossy.
Step 7 of 7

Squeeze half the lime over the pan, scoop the coconut rice into two bowls, and spoon the shrimp and all the pan sauce over the top. Finish with cilantro and the remaining lime in wedges.

🍗 Piri-Piri Chicken with Smoky Sausage and Peppers
Step 1 of 7

Whisk the harissa, smoked paprika, pepper flakes, garlic, vinegar, 3 tbsp olive oil, and 1 tsp salt into a loose piri-piri sauce. Spoon half of it over the chicken cutlets and turn them until slick; reserve the rest for finishing.

💡Thin cutlets take on marinade fast.
Step 2 of 7

Set a large skillet over medium heat and lay in the sausage coins in a single layer. Cook until the edges are browned and curled and a shallow layer of orange fat has rendered out, then scoop the sausage onto a plate and leave the fat behind.

💡That rendered fat is your searing medium.
Step 3 of 7

Raise the heat to medium-high and let the pan get hot enough that a drop of water skitters. Lay the cutlets in without crowding and press them flat with a spatula.

💡Work in two batches if the pan is tight.
Step 4 of 7

Sear undisturbed until the underside is deeply browned and the marinade has caramelized at the edges, then flip and cook until the center is just firm and the juices run clear.

💡Thin cutlets go from done to dry quickly.
Step 5 of 7

Move the chicken to a board to rest. Add the frozen peppers and onions straight to the hot pan and spread them out, letting them sit still so the water cooks off and the edges char.

💡Don't stir for the first few minutes.
Step 6 of 7

Return the sausage to the pan, add the juices from the chicken board, and squeeze in half the lemon. Toss for a minute until everything is glossy and smells sharp and smoky.

Step 7 of 7

Slice the chicken thick against the grain and pile it over the peppers right in the skillet. Spoon the reserved piri-piri over the top, scatter parsley, and serve with torn ciabatta for mopping and lemon wedges.

💡The raw sauce at the end is the whole point.
🥜 West African Chicken and Peanut Stew
Step 1 of 8

Pat the thighs very dry and season all over with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until it just starts to smoke, then lay the thighs in skin side down in two batches.

💡Dry skin is the difference between browning and steaming.
Step 2 of 8

Sear without touching them until the skin is deep golden and lifts cleanly from the pot, then flip for one more minute and transfer to a plate. Pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.

💡Let the skin release on its own.
Step 3 of 8

Drop the heat to medium and add the onions with a pinch of salt, scraping the browned bits off the bottom as they release moisture. Cook until they collapse and turn soft and translucent with golden edges.

💡Those stuck-on bits are pure flavor.
Step 4 of 8

Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder, and tomato paste and cook until the paste darkens from bright red to brick and smells toasty. Whisk the peanut butter into 1 cup of the broth in a measuring cup while this happens.

💡Pre-thinning the peanut butter stops it from clumping.
Step 5 of 8

Pour in the crushed tomatoes, the remaining broth, and the thinned peanut butter, then add the habanero halves and 1 1/2 tsp salt. Return the chicken and any juices to the pot, nestling the pieces so they are mostly submerged.

Step 6 of 8

Bring to a bare simmer, cover partially, and let it bubble gently, stirring every 10 minutes so the peanut butter doesn't catch on the bottom. The stew should barely blip, not boil.

💡A hard boil will make the sauce break and turn greasy.
Step 7 of 8

Add the sweet potatoes and simmer uncovered until they are tender at the center of a knife tip and the sauce has darkened and thickened enough to coat a spoon. Fish out and discard the habanero.

💡Taste before removing the chile if you want more heat.
Step 8 of 8

Stir in the spinach in handfuls until it wilts into the gravy, then taste and adjust with salt. Heat the rice pouches and serve the stew ladled over rice in wide bowls.

💡The stew tastes even better the next day.
🌶️ Sri Lankan Devilled Chicken
Step 1 of 7

Toss the chicken strips with the curry powder, pepper flakes, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp oil until every piece is rust colored. Let it sit on the counter while you cut the vegetables.

💡Room-temperature chicken sears instead of steams.
Step 2 of 7

Stir the sriracha, tomato paste, soy sauce, sugar, and 3 tbsp water into a smooth devilled sauce and park it by the stove. Start the rice packets in the microwave so they are ready at the end.

Step 3 of 7

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet or wok over high until it ripples and a strip of onion sizzles instantly. Add the cinnamon stick and let it toast until it smells sweet and woody.

💡The cinnamon perfumes the oil, so don't skip it.
Step 4 of 7

Spread the chicken in one layer and leave it completely alone until the underside is browned and crusted, then stir and cook until no pink remains on the outside.

💡Resist stirring early or you'll pull out water.
Step 5 of 7

Add the onion wedges and green pepper and stir-fry over high heat until they blister in spots but still have a distinct bite in the middle.

💡You want char, not softness.
Step 6 of 7

Add the garlic and ginger, toss for 30 seconds until fragrant, then pour in the devilled sauce. Toss constantly as it bubbles and reduces until it clings to the chicken and there is almost no liquid pooling in the pan.

💡Stop when the spoon leaves a clear trail.
Step 7 of 7

Pull out the cinnamon stick, taste for salt and heat, and serve over the hot jasmine rice while the sauce is still glossy.

🐟 Shoyu Ahi Poke Bowls
Step 1 of 7

Soak the shaved sweet onion in a bowl of ice water while you work so it loses its raw bite and turns crisp. Drain it well right before serving.

💡Ice water tames sharp onion in minutes.
Step 2 of 7

Pat the tuna completely dry and cut it against the grain into clean 3/4-inch cubes with a sharp knife, working quickly so the fish stays cold. Discard any tough silver sinew.

💡Partially frozen tuna cubes far more neatly.
Step 3 of 7

Toss the tuna gently with the Island Soyaki, sesame oil, and half the scallions using a spoon rather than your hands. Cover and refrigerate so it marinates without curing.

💡Any longer and the soy starts firming the fish.
Step 4 of 7

Microwave the jasmine rice packets per the package, fluff with a fork, and divide between two wide bowls. Let the rice cool for a couple of minutes so it doesn't cook the fish on contact.

💡Warm rice with cold fish is the classic contrast.
Step 5 of 7

Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together with 1 tsp water until it is thin enough to drizzle from a spoon. Slice the avocado and cucumber while it sits.

Step 6 of 7

Mound the marinated tuna over the rice and arrange the avocado, cucumber, and drained sweet onion around it in distinct sections. Pour any marinade left in the bowl over the rice.

💡Sections look better and let you build each bite.
Step 7 of 7

Zigzag the spicy mayo over the top, then finish with the remaining scallions, the Everything But The Bagel seasoning, and crumbled seaweed. Serve immediately while the fish is still cold.

🥓 Kielbasa and Caraway Cabbage with Mustard Cream
Step 1 of 8

Put the halved potatoes in a microwave-safe bowl with 2 tbsp water, cover, and microwave until a knife slides into one with only slight resistance. Drain them and leave them uncovered so the surfaces dry.

💡Par-cooking here is what keeps this under 35 minutes.
Step 2 of 8

Cook the bacon in a large cold skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are crisp and curled. Scoop the bacon out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat in the pan.

💡Starting cold renders the fat more completely.
Step 3 of 8

Turn the heat to medium-high and lay the kielbasa coins flat in the bacon fat. Sear undisturbed until the cut faces are dark brown and slightly domed, flip once, then move them to the bacon plate.

💡Flat contact is what builds the crust.
Step 4 of 8

Add the drained potatoes cut side down to the same pan and let them sit still until the flat sides are deeply golden and crusty. Push them to the edge of the pan.

💡Don't stir, or you'll get pale potatoes.
Step 5 of 8

Add the onion, caraway seeds, and paprika to the center and stir for a minute until the seeds smell toasted, then pile in the cabbage with 1 tsp salt. It will look like too much; press it down and let it wilt.

💡Cabbage loses half its volume almost immediately.
Step 6 of 8

Cook the cabbage, tossing every couple of minutes, until it is silky and browned in patches but still has some structure. Splash in the vinegar and sugar and scrape the bottom of the pan clean.

💡The vinegar deglazes and brightens all at once.
Step 7 of 8

Whisk the mustard and sour cream together with a splash of water and a grind of pepper until pourable. Return the sausage and bacon to the pan and toss just long enough to heat through.

Step 8 of 8

Divide between two plates, spoon the mustard cream over the top rather than stirring it in, and finish with a heavy scatter of dill.

💡Sour cream added off heat stays smooth instead of splitting.
🍜 Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodle Bowls
Step 1 of 8

Blitz the onions, garlic, and ginger in a food processor with a splash of water until you have a coarse, wet paste. If you have no processor, grate the ginger and garlic and mince the onion very fine.

💡This paste is the backbone of the broth.
Step 2 of 8

Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large pot over medium heat, add the onion paste and turmeric, and cook, stirring often, until the mixture darkens to a deep gold and the raw onion smell is gone. It should look jammy and pull away from the bottom.

💡Rushing this step leaves the broth tasting sharp.
Step 3 of 8

While the paste cooks, lower the eggs into a saucepan of boiling water and set a timer. Cook them, then shock them in ice water, peel, and halve.

💡Ice water makes the shells slip right off.
Step 4 of 8

Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt, add it to the onion paste, and stir over medium-high heat until the pieces are coated in gold and no longer pink on the outside.

💡You are coating, not browning.
Step 5 of 8

Pour in the broth, one can of the coconut milk, and the fish sauce. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat so the surface just shivers and cook uncovered until the chicken is tender enough to shred against the side of the pot.

💡A gentle simmer keeps the coconut milk from breaking.
Step 6 of 8

Whisk the cornstarch into the second can of coconut milk until completely smooth, then stir it into the pot. Simmer, stirring, until the broth thickens into a silky gravy that coats the back of a spoon.

💡Whisk before pouring or you'll get lumps.
Step 7 of 8

Cook the rice noodles in a separate pot of salted water according to the package until just tender, then drain and rinse briefly with cool water so they don't clump.

💡Rinsing stops the noodles from soaking up all your broth.
Step 8 of 8

Taste the broth and adjust with fish sauce, salt, and a squeeze of lime until it is savory and bright. Nest noodles in each bowl, ladle the chicken and gravy over, and top with egg halves, crispy fried onions, and lime wedges.

💡Add the crispy onions at the table so they stay crunchy.
🧄 Shkmeruli: Georgian Skillet Chicken in Garlic Milk
Step 1 of 8

Pat the thighs bone-dry with paper towels and season both sides hard with salt and pepper. Press each one flat with the heel of your hand so it will sit in full contact with the pan.

💡Any surface moisture steams the skin instead of crisping it.
Step 2 of 8

Set a cast iron skillet over medium heat and lay the thighs in skin side down, then set a smaller heavy pan directly on top to weigh them down. Cook without moving them until the fat has rendered out and the skin is deep amber and lacquer-crisp.

💡The weight is what gives shkmeruli its signature flat, crackling skin.
Step 3 of 8

Lift off the weight, flip the thighs, and cook the second side until the meat is firm and the juices run clear at the bone. Move the chicken to a plate skin side up while you build the sauce.

Step 4 of 8

Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat and drop the heat to low. Melt the butter in, then add the grated garlic and stir constantly until it smells sweet and looks pale gold but has taken on no color at all.

💡Browned garlic turns bitter and ruins the sauce.
Step 5 of 8

Stir in the coriander, fenugreek, paprika, and cayenne and let them bloom in the butter for a few seconds until fragrant. Pour in the milk and cream, scraping the bottom of the pan clean.

💡Fenugreek is the flavor that makes this taste Georgian rather than French.
Step 6 of 8

Raise the heat to medium-low and simmer the sauce, stirring often, until it thickens enough to leave a clear trail behind your spoon and turns pale ivory. Season it aggressively with salt and taste for garlic bite.

💡Keep it at a lazy blip; a hard boil will curdle the milk.
Step 7 of 8

Nestle the thighs back in skin side up so the sauce comes only halfway up the sides, keeping that crisp skin above the waterline. Spoon sauce over the meat and let it warm through.

💡Never submerge the skin you worked so hard for.
Step 8 of 8

Warm the naan directly over a burner or in a dry pan until blistered and pliable. Shower the chicken with cilantro and serve straight from the skillet with the bread for mopping.

💡The sauce is the point; the bread is the delivery system.
🍢 Nigerian Suya Steak with Yaji and Raw Onion
Step 1 of 8

Put the steak on a plate in the freezer to firm up so it slices cleanly. While it chills, drop the peanuts into a food processor or a zip bag and pulse or crush them to a coarse, sandy powder.

💡Stop before it turns to paste; the oil should stay locked in the crumbs.
Step 2 of 8

Stir the peanut powder together with the smoked paprika, cayenne, ginger, onion powder, garlic powder, crushed bouillon, and 1 tsp salt. Split this yaji into two piles and set half aside for finishing.

💡Half the yaji cooks on, half goes on raw for punch.
Step 3 of 8

Slice the chilled steak against the grain into strips about a quarter inch thick. Toss them with the oil, then rub in the first pile of yaji until every strip is coated and slightly damp.

💡Slicing against the grain is what keeps thin beef tender.
Step 4 of 8

Move an oven rack to the top slot and heat the broiler to high. Thread the strips onto skewers in loose ripples, or just spread them in a single layer on a foil-lined sheet with space between the pieces.

💡Crowding steams the beef and you lose the char.
Step 5 of 8

Broil until the edges blacken in spots and the spice crust looks dry and toasted, then flip and broil the second side until just done. While it cooks, drop the sliced onion into ice water so it turns crisp and loses its harsh edge.

💡Suya is meant to be well-charred outside, blushing inside.
Step 6 of 8

Flip the skewers and finish the second side under the broiler, watching closely since the peanut in the rub can go from toasted to burnt fast.

Step 7 of 8

Let the beef rest on the pan so the juices settle, then drain the onion and pat it dry. Shower the hot steak with most of the reserved yaji so it sticks to the surface.

💡Raw yaji on hot meat is the whole trick.
Step 8 of 8

Pile the steak on a platter with the cold onion and tomato slices scattered over the top. Serve with lime wedges and the last of the yaji in a dish for dredging bite by bite.

💡Eat it with your hands, standing up, the way it is sold on the street.
🐟 Basque Cod al Pil-Pil with Guindilla Chiles
Step 1 of 8

Salt the cod generously on all sides and set it on a rack or plate to sit at room temperature. Pat it completely dry before cooking, wiping away any beads of moisture the salt has pulled out.

💡Salting first firms the flesh and coaxes out the gelatin the sauce depends on.
Step 2 of 8

Pour the olive oil into a wide skillet or shallow casserole and add the garlic and chile rings. Set it over the lowest heat you can manage and let the garlic swim until it turns pale straw gold and the oil smells sweet.

💡If the garlic sizzles hard, the heat is too high; you want faint lazy bubbles.
Step 3 of 8

Scoop out the garlic and chiles with a slotted spoon and reserve them. Slide the cod into the warm oil skinned side down, making sure the oil comes at least halfway up each piece.

💡The oil should feel warm, not hot, when the fish goes in.
Step 4 of 8

Poach the fish over low heat, spooning oil over the top now and then, until the sides turn opaque white and small pearly bubbles gather around the edges. Flip carefully with a spatula and finish the second side until the flesh just begins to separate into flakes.

💡Those bubbles are the gelatin releasing; that is your sauce forming.
Step 5 of 8

Lift the cod out onto a warm plate and pull the pan off the heat. Let the oil cool for a couple of minutes so it stops shimmering, since a scorching pan will never emulsify.

💡Cooler oil emulsifies; hot oil splits.
Step 6 of 8

Tilt the pan and swirl it in steady circles, or work a fine sieve through the oil in small circles, until the clear oil clouds and thickens into a creamy, pale sauce the texture of loose mayonnaise. Keep going past the point where you think nothing is happening.

💡It turns all at once; sudden thickening means you did it right.
Step 7 of 8

Slide the cod back into the sauce along with any juices from the plate and warm it through over the lowest heat, tilting the pan to coat. Taste the sauce and correct with salt and a squeeze of lemon.

Step 8 of 8

Tear the bread into thick slabs and griddle them in a spoonful of the garlicky oil until crisp at the edges. Plate the cod with the torn piquillos, scatter the reserved garlic chips, chiles, and parsley over the top, and serve the bread alongside.

💡Nobody leaves pil-pil sauce in the pan.
🫑 Hungarian Beef Goulash with Caraway and Sweet Paprika
Step 1 of 8

Pat the beef cubes very dry and season them all over with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until it just smokes, then brown the beef in two or three uncrowded batches until every piece has a dark crust on at least two sides.

💡Crowded meat sweats grey instead of browning.
Step 2 of 8

Move the beef to a bowl and drop the heat to medium. Add the onions with a big pinch of salt and cook, scraping the fond off the bottom as they release their water, until they collapse into a soft golden mass.

💡Goulash is really an onion sauce; do not rush this.
Step 3 of 8

Pull the pot completely off the heat and let it lose its sizzle for a moment. Stir in both paprikas, the caraway, and the tomato paste so the residual heat blooms them into a thick red paste that coats the onions.

💡Paprika scorches in seconds over direct heat and turns acrid.
Step 4 of 8

Return the pot to medium, pour in the broth and vinegar, and add the bay leaves. Slide the beef and every drop of its resting juices back in, then season with 2 tsp salt.

Step 5 of 8

Bring it to a bare simmer where only a few bubbles break the surface, cover, and let it go low and slow, stirring once or twice. The beef should be nearly tender but still holding its shape when you check.

💡A rolling boil makes chuck stringy; keep it barely trembling.
Step 6 of 8

Add the potatoes and bell peppers, pushing them under the surface, and simmer uncovered so the gravy reduces. It is done when a knife slides into the beef with no resistance and the sauce coats the back of a spoon in a glossy red sheet.

💡A few potatoes breaking down is a good thing; it thickens the pot.
Step 7 of 8

Fish out the bay leaves, then taste and adjust with salt and another splash of vinegar if it tastes flat. Let the pot sit off the heat so the fat rises and the flavors settle.

💡Skim the surface fat if you want a cleaner-tasting gravy.
Step 8 of 8

Ladle into deep bowls and finish each with a spoonful of sour cream and a last pinch of sweet paprika. Stir the cream in at the table rather than into the pot.

💡Sour cream added to the whole pot can split on reheating.
🥣 Yucatecan Sopa de Lima with Crisp Tortilla Strips
Step 1 of 8

Season the thighs on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a saucepan over medium-high and sear the chicken until the undersides are golden brown, then flip once and pull the pan back to medium.

💡The browned bits on the bottom give this clear broth its backbone.
Step 2 of 8

Push the chicken aside, add the onion and tomatoes with a pinch of salt, and cook until the onion turns translucent and the tomatoes slump into the pan juices.

Step 3 of 8

Stir in the oregano, allspice, and cumin and let them toast until you can smell the allspice clearly. Pour in the broth, add the halved habanero, and bring it to a gentle simmer.

💡Allspice is the signature note of Yucatecan cooking; do not skip it.
Step 4 of 8

Simmer uncovered, skimming any foam, until the chicken is cooked through and shreds easily against the side of the pot with a fork.

💡Keep it at a lazy bubble so the broth stays clear rather than cloudy.
Step 5 of 8

While the soup simmers, heat the remaining oil in a skillet over medium-high and fry the tortilla strips in two batches, turning them, until they are stiff and pale gold. Drain them on paper towels and salt them right away.

💡Pull them a shade before they look done; they darken as they cool.
Step 6 of 8

Halve two of the limes and press them cut side down in a dry hot skillet until the surfaces are blackened and the juice inside is hot. Cut the remaining limes into wedges.

💡Charring pushes the lime from sour to smoky and slightly sweet.
Step 7 of 8

Pull the chicken out, shred it in big pieces, and return it to the pot. Fish out the habanero, then kill the heat and squeeze in the juice of the charred limes, tasting as you go until the broth is bracingly sour.

💡Add the lime off heat so it stays bright instead of turning bitter.
Step 8 of 8

Pile a handful of tortilla strips in the bottom of each bowl and ladle the hot soup over them. Finish with cilantro, extra strips on top, and lime wedges for squeezing at the table.

💡Serve immediately, while the strips still crunch.
🍳 Okinawan Pork and Tofu Champuru
Step 1 of 8

Wrap the tofu block in a clean towel, set a heavy pan on top, and let it press while you prep everything else. Tear it into rough bite-size chunks rather than cubing it so the craggy edges catch color.

💡Torn tofu has more surface area and browns far better than neat cubes.
Step 2 of 8

Lay the pork strips in a cold wok or large skillet and set it over medium heat so the fat renders slowly. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the strips are deep brown and crisp at the edges and the pan holds a good slick of fat.

💡Starting cold renders more fat, which is the cooking medium for everything else.
Step 3 of 8

Scoop the pork onto a plate and leave the fat behind. Raise the heat to medium-high and add the tofu chunks in one layer, letting them sit undisturbed until a golden crust forms before turning them.

💡If you stir too soon the tofu shreds; wait for the release.
Step 4 of 8

Push the tofu to one side, beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, and pour them into the empty half. Stir them in loose folds until barely set and still glossy, then slide them out onto the pork plate.

💡Undercook the eggs here since they finish in the hot pan later.
Step 5 of 8

Crank the heat to high and add the cabbage all at once. Let it sit against the metal without stirring so the cut edges blacken and blister, then toss and let it sit again until the leaves are wilted at the ribs but still snapping.

💡Real wok-style char is the difference between champuru and steamed cabbage.
Step 6 of 8

Return the pork and tofu to the pan, then pour in the soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, and umami seasoning around the edges so they hiss and caramelize. Toss everything hard until the sauce clings and the pan is nearly dry.

💡Saucing down the hot sides toasts the soy instead of steaming the food.
Step 7 of 8

Kill the heat and fold the eggs and scallions back in with a few gentle turns so the egg stays in soft ribbons. Grind over plenty of black pepper.

Step 8 of 8

Heat the jasmine rice according to the package while the pan rests. Serve the champuru over the rice and blizzard the whole thing with bonito flakes, which will curl and wave in the rising steam.

💡Add the bonito at the very last second so it moves at the table.
🍷 Alsatian Coq au Riesling with Bacon and Mushrooms
Step 1 of 8

Set a heavy skillet over medium heat and render the lardons, stirring now and then, until they are crisp and have given up a pool of fat. Lift them out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat in the pan.

💡Start them in a cold pan so they render rather than seize.
Step 2 of 8

Pat the thighs dry, season with salt and pepper, and sear them in the bacon fat over medium-high without moving them until the undersides are mahogany. Flip, brown briefly, and move them to a plate; they will finish in the sauce.

💡You want color, not doneness, at this stage.
Step 3 of 8

Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them completely alone until they stop squeaking, release their water, and take on dark caramelized faces. Salt them only after they have browned.

💡Salting early pulls out water and stalls the browning.
Step 4 of 8

Drop the heat to medium, add the butter, shallots, and thyme, and cook until the shallots go soft and translucent. Sprinkle the flour over everything and stir until it disappears and smells faintly toasty.

Step 5 of 8

Pour in the Riesling and scrape every browned scrap off the bottom of the pan. Let it bubble briskly until it has reduced by about half and the sharp alcohol smell has cooked off, and start your noodle water while you wait.

💡Taste the wine first; if you would not drink it, do not cook with it.
Step 6 of 8

Whisk in the cream and Dijon, then nestle the chicken back in along with its juices. Turn the heat to low and simmer gently, spooning sauce over the thighs, until the sauce coats a spoon and the chicken is cooked through.

💡Keep it under a boil so the cream stays smooth.
Step 7 of 8

Boil the noodles in well-salted water until just tender, drain them, and toss with a knob of butter and a pinch of pepper. Taste the sauce and adjust with salt and a little more mustard if it needs sharpening.

Step 8 of 8

Spoon the noodles into warm shallow bowls, lay the chicken over them, and pour the sauce and mushrooms across the top. Scatter the crisp lardons and parsley over everything just before it goes to the table.

💡Adding the bacon at the end keeps it crunchy against the sauce.
🌽 Colombian Chicken Sancocho with Aji Picante
Step 1 of 8

Season the chicken hard with salt and pepper and pile it into a large stockpot with the onion, half the scallions, the garlic, one whole jalapeno, the cumin, the turmeric, and the cilantro stems. Cover with about 12 cups of cold water.

💡Starting in cold water draws more flavor out of the bones.
Step 2 of 8

Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then immediately drop it to a bare simmer. Skim off the grey foam that rises in the first few minutes until the surface runs clear.

💡Skimming now is what gives sancocho its clean golden broth.
Step 3 of 8

Cover partially and simmer gently so the surface only trembles, until the chicken is tender enough that the meat pulls back from the bone ends. Taste the broth and season it well with salt.

💡A hard boil will cloud the broth and dry out the meat.
Step 4 of 8

While it simmers, make the aji: finely chop the cilantro leaves, the remaining scallions, and the second jalapeno, then stir them together with the juice of one lime, a splash of water, and a big pinch of salt. Let it sit so the flavors marry.

💡The aji should taste sharper and saltier than seems reasonable on its own.
Step 5 of 8

Add the plantain chunks to the pot and simmer uncovered until they are starting to soften but still hold together firmly at the center when pierced.

💡Green plantain releases starch that begins thickening the broth.
Step 6 of 8
