Add the potatoes and corn rounds, pushing them under the liquid, and simmer until the potatoes are completely tender and a few edges have crumbled into the broth, thickening it to a light body.

💡Those disintegrating potato edges are the goal, not a mistake.
Step 7 of 8

Fish out the whole jalapeno and any loose bones, then pull the chicken pieces to a board if you want and slip the skin off. Return the meat to the pot in large pieces and taste the broth one last time for salt.

💡Leaving big bone-in pieces is traditional; boneless is easier for lunches.
Step 8 of 8

Let the pot rest off the heat so the flavors settle and the fat rises to skim if you like. Ladle into wide bowls with a piece of everything in each, and pass the aji and remaining lime wedges at the table.

💡Every bowl should get chicken, plantain, corn, and potato.
🥢 Cantonese Steamed Cod with Sizzling Ginger-Scallion Oil
Step 1 of 8

Set a rack or a pair of chopsticks inside a wide lidded skillet or wok, add water to just below the rack, and bring it to a hard boil over high heat. Meanwhile pat the fish completely dry and salt it lightly on both sides.

💡The plate must sit above the water, never in it
Step 2 of 8

Scatter the smashed ginger and scallion whites over a heatproof plate that fits inside the pan, lay the fillets on top, and splash them with the Shaoxing wine. Lower the plate onto the rack, cover, and steam over medium-high.

Step 3 of 8

While the fish steams, drop the julienned ginger and scallion greens into a bowl of cold water so they curl and crisp, then drain them right before serving.

Step 4 of 8

Stir the soy sauce, sugar, and a splash of water together in a small saucepan and warm it over low heat just until the sugar dissolves and the sauce smells round instead of sharp. Keep it hot.

Step 5 of 8

Tuck the bok choy halves around the plate for the last stretch of steaming and microwave the jasmine rice according to the bag. The fish is done when it flakes into thick opaque petals at the very center.

💡Pull it the moment it flakes, or it turns cottony
Step 6 of 8

Lift the plate out carefully and tip off the cloudy pooled liquid, then discard the smashed aromatics underneath. Pile the drained ginger and scallion threads over the fillets.

Step 7 of 8

Heat the peanut oil in a small pan over high heat until it shimmers and a single scallion shred sizzles violently on contact, then pour it straight over the aromatics so the whole plate crackles.

💡This step is the entire dish, so get the oil truly ripping
Step 8 of 8

Pour the warm soy mixture around the base of the fillets rather than over the top, finish with the sesame oil and cilantro, and serve with the rice and bok choy.

🫚 Dhaba-Style Chicken Karahi with Crushed Coriander
Step 1 of 7

Melt the ghee in a wok or heavy skillet over high heat until it ripples and thins out. Add the chicken in a single uncrowded layer and leave it alone until the undersides are browned and the edges have caught color.

💡Crowding steams the meat and you lose the fond
Step 2 of 7

Stir in the crushed coriander seeds, garlic, grated ginger, and slit chiles and toss constantly until the garlic smells sweet and the coriander turns fragrant and toasty.

Step 3 of 7

Add the tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, and a generous pinch of salt. Cook over medium-high, mashing the tomatoes against the pan every couple of minutes, until they collapse into a thick masala and rust-colored ghee pools at the edges.

💡Oil separating at the rim means the masala is cooked
Step 4 of 7

Splash in a few tablespoons of water, scrape the bottom clean, then cover and drop the heat to medium-low so the chicken finishes through to the center in the steam.

Step 5 of 7

While it cooks, warm the naan directly over a gas flame or in a dry skillet over medium-high, turning it until it puffs and picks up dark blistered spots.

Step 6 of 7

Uncover, raise the heat to high, and stir almost constantly as the sauce tightens, darkens a shade, and clings to each piece of chicken instead of running off it.

💡This is the bhuna, and it is where the flavor concentrates
Step 7 of 7

Kill the heat, shower on the garam masala, the julienned ginger, and most of the cilantro, and let it sit a minute before serving straight from the pan with the naan and the last of the cilantro.

🧀 Sardinian Saffron Sausage Malloreddus with Pecorino
Step 1 of 8

Crumble the saffron threads into a small bowl with a few tablespoons of very hot water and leave them to steep while you build the sauce. Put a large pot of heavily salted water on to boil.

💡The soaking water should turn deep orange
Step 2 of 8

Heat a wide skillet over medium-high with a slick of olive oil, add the sausage in one flat slab, and let it sit untouched until the underside is deeply browned before breaking it into craggy pieces.

Step 3 of 8

Add the onion, fennel seeds, and pepper flakes and cook over medium until the onion is soft and translucent, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.

Step 4 of 8

Pour in the white wine, scrape every browned bit off the bottom, and simmer hard until the pan smells sweet rather than boozy and the liquid has nearly disappeared.

Step 5 of 8

Crush the tomatoes to shreds with your hands straight into the pan, add the saffron and its water and a good pinch of salt, and simmer over low, stirring now and then, until the sauce turns dark brick red and mounds on the spoon.

Step 6 of 8

While the sauce reduces, boil the pasta until it is still noticeably firm at the core, then scoop out a mug of the starchy water before draining.

💡Pull it a minute early since it finishes in the sauce
Step 7 of 8

Tip the pasta into the skillet with a splash of pasta water and half the pecorino, and toss over medium heat until the sauce turns glossy and coats every ridge.

Step 8 of 8

Take the pan off the heat, tear in the basil, and serve with the remaining pecorino piled on top.

🫓 Egyptian Chicken Fattah with Garlic-Vinegar Tomato Sauce
Step 1 of 8

Pile the chicken into a large pot with the quartered onion, smashed garlic, cinnamon stick, cardamom, and bay leaves, cover with cold water by an inch, and bring to a boil over high heat. Skim off the gray foam that rises as it comes up.

💡Skimming is the difference between cloudy and clean broth
Step 2 of 8

Drop the heat to a bare simmer, partially cover, and cook until the meat is tender and pulling back from the ends of the bones. Meanwhile rinse the rice under cold water until it runs clear and tear the naan into shards.

Step 3 of 8

Lift the chicken onto a foil-lined sheet pan and strain the broth into a bowl, discarding the spices and keeping the broth hot. Brush the chicken with ghee, salt it, and broil on high until the skin is blistered, brown, and crackling.

Step 4 of 8

In a saucepan, toast the drained rice in a couple tablespoons of ghee over medium heat, stirring, until the grains turn chalky white and smell nutty like popcorn.

Step 5 of 8

Pour in hot strained broth to cover the rice by about a finger's width, season with salt, bring to a boil, then clamp on the lid and cook on the lowest heat until every drop is absorbed. Rest it off the heat, still covered, before fluffing.

💡No peeking, and no stirring once the lid is on
Step 6 of 8

Toss the naan shards with a little ghee on a sheet pan and bake or broil them until they are dry, golden, and audibly crisp when you tap one.

Step 7 of 8

Sizzle the minced garlic with the coriander and cumin in the remaining ghee over medium heat until the garlic is pale gold and sharply fragrant but not browned, then add the tomato sauce and a ladle of broth and simmer until it darkens and thickens.

💡Browned garlic turns bitter, so pull it early
Step 8 of 8

Off the heat, stir the vinegar into the tomato sauce and taste; it should be aggressively tangy. Layer the crisp bread in a wide dish, moisten it with hot broth, pile on the rice and then the chicken, and pour the sauce over everything before showering with parsley.

🍺 Bavarian Jagerschnitzel with Bacon-Mushroom Gravy
Step 1 of 8

Lay each chop between two sheets of plastic wrap and pound it with a heavy pan from the center outward until it is thin and even all over. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

💡Thin and even means it cooks through before the crust burns
Step 2 of 8

Set out three shallow dishes of flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then crumbs, pressing lightly rather than packing them on, and rest them on a rack.

💡A loose crumb coat is what lets the crust puff
Step 3 of 8

Render the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until the fat has pooled and the pieces are crisp and deep brown, then scoop the bacon out and leave the fat behind.

Step 4 of 8

Turn the heat to medium-high, spread the mushrooms in the bacon fat in a single layer, and leave them completely still until the undersides are dark brown. Add the onion and cook until it softens and turns translucent.

💡Salt the mushrooms only after they brown
Step 5 of 8

Sprinkle in the umami seasoning and a spoonful of the leftover flour, stir for a minute, then pour in the broth and scrape the pan clean. Simmer until it reduces by about half, add the cream, and hold it over the lowest heat.

Step 6 of 8

In a second wide skillet, heat a generous layer of olive oil with the butter over medium-high until the butter foams and the foam just begins to subside. Slide in the cutlets and tilt the pan to spoon hot fat over the tops as they fry.

Step 7 of 8

Flip once the underside is even golden brown and cook the second side until it matches and the crust has visibly lifted away from the meat in blisters.

Step 8 of 8

Rest the cutlets on a rack for a minute so they stay crisp, stir the bacon back into the gravy, and serve the gravy in a puddle beside each schnitzel with lemon wedges for squeezing.

💡Gravy on top turns the crust to mush
🐑 Uyghur Cumin Lamb with Blistered Onions
Step 1 of 8

Toss the sliced lamb with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch until every piece is slick, then leave it to sit while you cut the vegetables.

💡The cornstarch is what gives you that velvety restaurant texture
Step 2 of 8

Toast the cumin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking constantly, until they darken a shade and smell sharply fragrant. Tip them onto a board and crush them coarsely with the flat of a knife along with the chili flakes.

💡Crush, do not grind, so you get crunchy pops of spice
Step 3 of 8

Warm the naan in a low oven or dry skillet while the pan comes up to temperature, then wrap it in a towel to stay soft.

Step 4 of 8

Heat a wok or heavy skillet over the highest heat until it faintly smokes, add the oil, and lay the lamb out in one layer. Leave it completely undisturbed so it sears rather than steams.

Step 5 of 8

Stir-fry hard until no pink remains and the edges are crisped and lacquered, then scrape the lamb out onto a plate.

Step 6 of 8

Throw the onion and bell pepper into the same searing pan and let them sit still until the edges blacken and blister before tossing them once or twice; they should stay crunchy in the middle.

Step 7 of 8

Return the lamb with the garlic and most of the crushed cumin and chili, and toss constantly until the spices coat everything and the pan smells overwhelmingly of cumin.

Step 8 of 8

Kill the heat, fold in the cilantro and the last of the spice mix, and serve straight from the pan with the warm naan for tearing and scooping.

🧅 Cuban Bistec Encebollado with Black Beans and Rice
Step 1 of 8

Mash the garlic with a big pinch of salt into a paste, then whisk it with the juice of two limes, the juice of the orange, the cumin, and the oregano. That sour-orange mix is your mojo.

Step 2 of 8

Pour half the mojo over the steaks and turn them to coat, then toss the onion rings with the other half in a separate bowl. Let both sit while you cook the beans.

💡Any longer in the acid and the meat goes chalky
Step 3 of 8

Soften the bell pepper in olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat until it slumps and smells sweet, then add the black beans with their liquid and the bay leaf and simmer until the liquid thickens around them.

Step 4 of 8

Set a cast iron skillet over high heat until it just begins to smoke. Pat the steaks bone dry, shaking off the marinade, and lay them in without crowding.

💡Wet meat will never brown, so dry them well
Step 5 of 8

Sear undisturbed until a dark crust forms and the edges look cooked partway up the side.

Step 6 of 8

Flip and cook just until the second side browns, then move the steaks to a plate to rest; thin steaks go from juicy to leathery in seconds.

Step 7 of 8

Dump the onions and their mojo into the hot pan, scraping up every browned bit, and cook over medium-high until they go limp and golden at the edges and the liquid reduces to a glaze. Heat the rice pouches while they cook.

Step 8 of 8

Pile the onions and pan juices over the rested steaks, squeeze the last lime over the top, and serve with the beans, rice, and a scatter of cilantro.

🥥 Kuku Paka: Swahili Coast Charred Chicken in Coconut Curry
Step 1 of 9

Blitz the garlic, ginger, chiles, and cilantro stems with the juice of one lime and a splash of water into a rough paste. Rub half of it over the chicken along with half the turmeric and plenty of salt.

💡Let it sit while the broiler heats and the onions cook
Step 2 of 9

Heat the broiler on high and arrange the chicken skin side up on a foil-lined sheet pan. Broil until the skin is blistered, deeply charred in patches, and the fat has rendered out. It does not need to be cooked through yet.

💡Char is the whole point, so let a few spots go black
Step 3 of 9

While the chicken broils, cook the onion in olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it is soft and just turning golden at the edges.

Step 4 of 9

Add the remaining spice paste with the rest of the turmeric and the coriander and fry, stirring, until the raw garlic smell disappears and the paste darkens and tightens against the pot.

Step 5 of 9

Stir in the grated tomatoes and cook them down until they go jammy and the oil separates out and slicks the surface.

Step 6 of 9

Pour in both cans of coconut milk, season with salt, and bring it to a bare quiver over medium-low. Do not let it reach a rolling boil or the sauce will break.

Step 7 of 9

Nestle the charred chicken and every drop of its pan juices into the sauce and simmer uncovered, spooning sauce over the tops now and then, until the meat pulls easily from the bone and the sauce coats a spoon.

Step 8 of 9

Finish off the heat with the juice of another lime and most of the chopped cilantro leaves, then taste hard for salt, heat, and acid and push whichever one is lagging.

💡It should taste bright, not just rich
Step 9 of 9

Serve over the cooked basmati with the remaining cilantro and lime wedges on the side.

🍗 Three-Cup Chicken with Charred Ginger and Thai Basil
Step 1 of 7

Pat the chicken chunks very dry and season them with black pepper only, since the soy sauce brings all the salt this dish needs. Stir the soy sauce, wine, and brown sugar together in a small bowl so the sauce is ready to hit a hot pan.

💡Season with pepper now, salt at the very end if at all.
Step 2 of 7

Pour the sesame oil into a wok or heavy 12-inch skillet and set it over medium-low, then add the ginger coins in a single layer. Fry them gently until the edges curl, turn pale gold, and go slightly papery.

💡Low and slow here; scorched sesame oil turns bitter.
Step 3 of 7

Add the whole garlic cloves and dried chiles and keep the heat at medium-low, rolling them through the oil until the garlic is blistered and golden on two sides and the chiles darken. Fish the garlic and ginger onto a plate if they are browning faster than that.

💡Whole cloves go sweet and creamy inside.
Step 4 of 7

Crank the heat to medium-high, add the chicken in one layer, and leave it completely alone until the undersides are browned and release from the pan. Toss once and let the second side color.

💡Resist stirring or you get gray meat, not brown.
Step 5 of 7

Pour in the soy mixture, let it come to a hard bubble, then drop the heat to medium and simmer, tossing every minute or so, until the liquid reduces to a syrup that coats every chunk and pools thickly at the bottom. Heat the jasmine rice while this reduces.

💡Pull it when the glaze streaks the pan and closes slowly.
Step 6 of 7

Kill the heat, pile in the scallion batons and all the basil at once, and toss hard for a minute until the leaves collapse into the glaze and go glossy dark green. Taste and add a splash more soy if it needs it.

💡Off-heat keeps the basil perfumed instead of stewed.
Step 7 of 7

Spoon the chicken over bowls of hot jasmine rice, scraping every bit of glaze and the sweet garlic cloves out of the pan. Eat immediately while the basil is still fragrant.

🫒 Poulet Provencal with Olives, Fennel and Orange
Step 1 of 8

Heat the oven to 425F. Pat the thighs bone-dry, season both sides hard with salt and pepper, and set them skin side up on the counter while the oven comes up.

💡Wet skin steams; dry skin shatters.
Step 2 of 8

Film an oven-safe 10-inch skillet with olive oil over medium-high and lay the thighs in skin side down. Leave them completely untouched until the skin is deep golden and lifts cleanly from the pan when you nudge it.

💡If it sticks, it isn't ready to turn.
Step 3 of 8

Flip the thighs for one minute, then move them to a plate skin side up and pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the fat. Drop the heat to medium and lay the fennel wedges in cut side down.

Step 4 of 8

Cook the fennel over medium without moving it until the flat faces are deeply caramelized and the wedges are just starting to bend. Smash the garlic and strip the orange zest while it colors.

💡Fennel goes sweet and almost meaty when browned this hard.
Step 5 of 8

Add the garlic, anchovies, crushed fennel seeds, and herbes de Provence and stir over medium until the anchovies dissolve into the fat and the pan smells like a pine forest. Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom clean.

💡The anchovy melts away completely; nobody will find it.
Step 6 of 8

Once the wine has reduced by half and lost its raw smell, stir in the tomatoes, olives, artichokes, orange zest strips, and orange juice. Nestle the thighs back in skin side up so the skin sits proud of the liquid.

💡Keep the skin above the sauce line to stay crisp.
Step 7 of 8

Slide the skillet into the oven and roast until the tomatoes burst and slump, the sauce is glossy, and the thickest thigh reads 175F. Slice and toast the baguette while it roasts.

Step 8 of 8

Let the pan rest so the juices settle, then taste the sauce and adjust the salt, remembering the olives and anchovy already brought plenty. Serve straight from the skillet with bread for the sauce.

💡The orange peel is for perfume, not eating.
🍤 Chupe de Camarones, Chilean Shrimp and Bread Chowder
Step 1 of 8

Tear the bread into rough pieces, drop them into a bowl with the milk, and press them under so they soak through. Meanwhile pat the shrimp dry and season them with salt and 1/2 tsp of the merken.

💡The bread is the thickener; no flour anywhere in this.
Step 2 of 8

Melt the butter in an oven-safe skillet or small Dutch oven over medium and add the onion with a big pinch of salt. Cook it slowly, stirring now and then, until it is fully soft and translucent with no browning at all.

💡Color here would muddy the clean red of the finished chowder.
Step 3 of 8

Stir in the garlic, the remaining merken, and the sweet paprika and cook over medium until the fat stains brick red and smells toasted. Do not let the paprika catch on the bottom.

💡Blooming the chiles in fat is what makes it taste Chilean.
Step 4 of 8

Scrape in the soaked bread with all its milk plus the broth, then mash and stir with a wooden spoon over medium until the bread disappears into a thick, spoon-coating porridge. Add a splash more milk if it gets stiffer than loose oatmeal.

💡Keep it moving; the bottom scorches fast.
Step 5 of 8

Stir in the cream, taste, and season aggressively with salt and pepper since the base is starchy and needs it. Turn on the broiler to high.

Step 6 of 8

Drop the heat to low, nestle the shrimp into the surface of the chowder, and let them poach gently until they turn opaque and curl into loose C shapes. Do not stir them around.

💡Tight O-shaped shrimp are already overcooked.
Step 7 of 8

Scatter the mozzarella over the top and slide the pan 6 inches under the broiler until the cheese is molten with blistered brown spots.

💡Watch it the whole time; it goes from gold to black in seconds.
Step 8 of 8

Let the chowder settle so it stops volcano-bubbling, then shower it with cilantro and serve it straight from the pan with spoons.

🦐 Low-Country Shrimp and Sausage over Unexpected Cheddar Grits
Step 1 of 9

Bring 5 cups of the broth plus 2 cups water and 1 1/2 tsp salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pot over high heat. Rain the grits in slowly with one hand while whisking constantly with the other.

💡Whisking during the pour is the only way to avoid lumps.
Step 2 of 9

Drop the heat to the lowest simmer you can hold, cover, and cook the grits until they are creamy and no longer feel sandy on your tongue, whisking every 10 minutes and scraping the corners. Prep everything else while they cook.

💡Taste, do not time; sandy grits are undercooked grits.
Step 3 of 9

Put the bacon in a large cold skillet and set it over medium so the fat renders out slowly. Cook until the pieces are crisp and the pan holds a generous slick of fat, then lift the bacon out to a paper towel and leave the fat behind.

💡Starting cold renders more fat and burns less.
Step 4 of 9

Raise the heat to medium-high and lay the sausage coins in the bacon fat in one layer. Sear without stirring until the cut faces are caramelized and the edges cup upward, then push them to one side.

Step 5 of 9

Add the bell pepper and scallion whites and cook over medium-high until softened with charred edges, stirring in the garlic for the last minute so it perfumes without burning. Season the shrimp with salt and pepper while this happens.

💡Garlic goes in last; it burns in half the time peppers need.
Step 6 of 9

Add the shrimp in a single layer and leave them undisturbed until the undersides turn pink, then toss and cook just until opaque through and curled. Pull the pan off the heat immediately.

💡They will keep cooking in the hot gravy, so undershoot.
Step 7 of 9

Stir the hot sauce, the juice of the whole lemon, the remaining 1 cup broth, and half the bacon into the skillet, scraping the browned bits loose into what is now a loose, peppery pan gravy. Taste for salt.

💡The broth plus fond is the gravy; nothing else needed.
Step 8 of 9

Kill the heat under the grits and beat in the butter and Unexpected Cheddar until glossy and pourable, adding a splash of water if they have gone stiff. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.

💡Off the heat so the cheese emulsifies instead of breaking.
Step 9 of 9

Ladle the grits into wide bowls, spoon the shrimp and sausage with all their gravy over the top, and finish with the remaining bacon and the scallion greens.

🌶️ Nepali Chicken Chhoila with Mustard Oil and Timur
Step 1 of 8

Toast the timur and fenugreek seeds in a dry skillet over medium, shaking constantly, until they smell nutty and the fenugreek darkens one shade. Crush them coarsely in a mortar or under a heavy pan and set aside.

💡Fenugreek turns bitter the second it goes past golden brown.
Step 2 of 8

Pat the thighs completely dry and rub them with the ginger-garlic paste, the turmeric, half the ground chili, and a heavy pinch of salt. Set a cast iron skillet over medium-high until it smokes faintly.

Step 3 of 8

Lay the thighs down with just a slick of oil and leave them absolutely still until the undersides are blackened in patches and the meat releases from the pan on its own.

💡You want real char, not color; this is a grill dish indoors.
Step 4 of 8

Flip and cook the second side until the thickest part reads 175F and the juices run clear. Sliver the onion and chop the cilantro while it finishes.

Step 5 of 8

Rest the chicken on a board, then hack it into rough 3/4-inch cubes, blackened edges and all, and pile it into a large bowl with the onion and cilantro.

💡Resting first keeps the juices in the bowl, not on the board.
Step 6 of 8

Heat the mustard oil in a small pan over medium-high until it shimmers and smells sharp and pungent, then add the dried chiles, the remaining ground chili, and the crushed timur-fenugreek. Swirl until it foams and turns dark red.

💡Mustard oil must be heated to smoking to lose its raw bite.
Step 7 of 8

Pour the sizzling oil straight over the chicken so it crackles, add the juice of the whole lemon and a good pinch of salt, and toss hard until every cube is stained red and slick. Taste and push the salt and lemon further than feels polite.

💡Chhoila should be loud, sour, and salty.
Step 8 of 8

Warm the naan directly in the hot dry skillet over medium-high until puffed and spotted on both sides, then serve alongside the chicken.

🍝 Pasta con le Sarde, Sicilian Sardines with Fennel and Saffron
Step 1 of 8

Bring a large pot of aggressively salted water to a boil over high heat. Crumble the saffron into 1/3 cup of very hot water in a mug and drop the raisins in to steep and plump.

💡Blooming saffron in hot water pulls out far more color.
Step 2 of 8

Toast the breadcrumbs with 1 tbsp olive oil in a dry skillet over medium, stirring nonstop, until they are sandy gold and audibly crisp. Scrape them onto a plate.

💡These are the Sicilian answer to parmesan; do not skip them.
Step 3 of 8

Add the pine nuts to the same pan over medium and toast until freckled brown, then tip them out with the breadcrumbs.

💡Pull them early; they scorch off residual heat.
Step 4 of 8

Add a generous glug of olive oil to the pan, raise to medium-high, and cook the diced fennel and onion with a pinch of salt until softened and browning at the edges. Drop the pasta into the boiling water as soon as they go in.

💡Slightly browned fennel is sweeter than pale fennel.
Step 5 of 8

Stir in the anchovies, tomato paste, and red pepper flakes and mash them into the vegetables over medium until the anchovies dissolve and the paste darkens from red to brick.

Step 6 of 8

Pour in the saffron water with the raisins plus a ladle of pasta water and simmer over medium until it looks like a loose, golden-orange sauce. Break two tins of sardines into big flakes and fold them in gently so some pieces stay whole.

💡Fold, don't stir, or the sardines turn to paste.
Step 7 of 8

Drain the pasta one minute shy of al dente and drop it straight into the pan with another splash of pasta water. Toss over medium-high until the sauce clings to every strand and the pasta is just al dente.

💡Starchy pasta water is what makes it cling.
Step 8 of 8

Off the heat, squeeze in half the lemon, taste for salt, and pile it into bowls. Top with the reserved tin of sardines, the fennel fronds, and a heavy shower of breadcrumbs and pine nuts.

🥘 Trinidadian Brown Stew Chicken with Burnt Sugar
Step 1 of 8

Chop the cilantro, scallions, garlic, thyme, and half the scotch bonnet together into a rough wet paste with 2 tbsp water, or pulse it in a small food processor. Rub two-thirds of this green seasoning and 1 tsp salt all over the chicken and leave it to sit while you prep the rest.

💡Green seasoning is the backbone of every Trini pot.
Step 2 of 8

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium, add the brown sugar, and let it melt mostly undisturbed until it darkens to the color of dark molasses, foams, and starts to smoke faintly. Pull it one shade before you think you should.

💡This burnt sugar is the whole dish; black and acrid means start over.
Step 3 of 8

Scrape the marinade off the chicken and reserve it, then lower the pieces into the bubbling caramel skin side down; they will hiss and seize. Turn them with tongs over medium heat until every side is coated deep mahogany.

💡Wet marinade in hot caramel will spatter, so use tongs and stand back.
Step 4 of 8

Add the onion and bell pepper and cook over medium until they slump and pick up the dark color from the pot, scraping the bottom as they release moisture.

Step 5 of 8

Stir in the reserved green seasoning, soy sauce, ketchup, broth, and the remaining scotch bonnet half left whole. Scrape the bottom of the pot completely clean and bring it to a simmer.

💡Whole chile in the pot gives fruity perfume without much burn.
Step 6 of 8

Cover, drop to low, and simmer until the chicken pulls easily from the bone with a fork. Heat the rice pouches during the last few minutes.

💡A bare blip, not a boil, or the meat tightens up.
Step 7 of 8

Uncover, fish out the chile, raise the heat to medium-high, and reduce the gravy until it turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon. Spoon it over the chicken as it thickens.

Step 8 of 8

Taste for salt, remembering the soy sauce, and serve the chicken over jasmine rice with the gravy poured generously over everything.

🍛 Kashmiri Rogan Josh with Fennel and Black Cardamom
Step 1 of 9

Pat the lamb cubes very dry and season them with salt. Melt the ghee in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until it shimmers, then add the whole spices and bay leaves and fry until the cardamom pods puff and the kitchen smells like a spice shop.

💡Whole spices go in first so the fat carries their perfume everywhere.
Step 2 of 9

Add half the lamb in a single uncrowded layer and sear over medium-high, undisturbed, until the underside is deep brown and lifts cleanly, then turn to brown a second face. Transfer to a bowl and repeat with the rest.

💡Two batches; crowded lamb steams gray and never browns.
Step 3 of 9

Drop the heat to medium-low and sprinkle the asafoetida into the fat for a few seconds, then whisk in the Kashmiri chili powder along with 1/4 cup water so it turns into a glossy red paste instead of scorching.

💡The splash of water is what keeps the chile from burning bitter.
Step 4 of 9

Pull the pot off the burner for a moment, then stir in the whisked yogurt a few spoonfuls at a time, stirring constantly between additions, until the sauce is smooth and uniformly brick red.

💡Adding it cold or all at once will split the yogurt into curds.
Step 5 of 9

Return the lamb and every drop of its juices to the pot, then stir in the ground fennel, dry ginger, 2 tsp salt, and 2 cups water. Bring it back to a lazy simmer over medium.

Step 6 of 9

Cover and hold it at the barest simmer, stirring and scraping the bottom every 10 minutes so the yogurt doesn't catch. The surface should blip occasionally, never roll.

💡If it is bubbling hard, your low is too high.
Step 7 of 9

Uncover, raise to medium-low, and simmer until the lamb is fork-tender and the gravy has reduced to a thick rust-red sauce with a distinct slick of red oil pooling on the surface. That rising oil is the classic sign it is done.

💡Skim the oil or stir it back in, cook's choice.
Step 8 of 9

Stir in the garam masala off the heat, taste for salt, and let the pot rest while you heat the rice pouches and warm the naan in a dry skillet over medium-high.

💡Garam masala goes in at the end so it stays fragrant.
Step 9 of 9

Fish out the cinnamon stick and the black cardamom pods, then ladle the lamb over basmati in wide bowls with naan on the side.

💡Black cardamom pods are not for eating whole.
🦐 Singapore Chili Shrimp with Egg Ribbon Gravy
Step 1 of 8

Pat the shrimp completely dry and season them lightly with salt, then spread them on a plate so they are not touching. Leave them out while you build the sauce so they lose their fridge chill.

💡Dry shrimp sear instead of steam.
Step 2 of 8

Stir the sweet chili sauce, ketchup, sriracha, soy sauce and 1/2 cup water together in a bowl until smooth. Slice the scallions and grate the garlic and ginger while you are at the board.

Step 3 of 8

Heat a wide skillet over medium-high with a slick of olive oil, then add the garlic and ginger. Stir constantly until they smell sweet and the garlic just turns pale gold at the edges.

💡Do not let the garlic brown.
Step 4 of 8

Pour in the sauce mixture and bring it to a hard bubble. Simmer, stirring now and then, until it darkens from orange to brick red and coats the back of a spoon.

Step 5 of 8

Slide the shrimp in one layer and cook, flipping once, until they curl into loose C-shapes and turn opaque all the way through. Red shrimp go fast, so pull them the moment the last gray streak disappears.

💡A tight O means overcooked.
Step 6 of 8

Stir the cornstarch slurry and drizzle it in, swirling the pan until the gravy turns glossy. Then pour the beaten egg in a thin stream across the surface, wait without stirring until it sets into ribbons, and fold it in gently.

Step 7 of 8

While the gravy finishes, toast the naan in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame until it puffs and picks up blistered black spots. Tear it into big mopping pieces.

Step 8 of 8

Shower the shrimp with scallions and squeeze a lime wedge over the whole pan. Serve straight from the skillet with the charred naan alongside.

🐟 Mustard-Dill Salmon with Smashed Dill Potatoes
Step 1 of 8

Cover the potatoes with heavily salted cold water, bring to a boil, and cook until a paring knife slides into the biggest one with zero resistance. Start the sauce while they bubble away.

💡Salt the water like the sea.
Step 2 of 8

Whisk both mustards, the honey and the vinegar into a thick, mayonnaise-glossy sauce, then fold in a large handful of chopped dill. Let it sit so the mustard mellows.

Step 3 of 8

Toss the cucumber coins with a pinch of salt and a splash more vinegar and slide them into the fridge to crisp and turn translucent at the edges.

Step 4 of 8

Pat the salmon bone-dry and season both sides. Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high until it shimmers and thins, then lay the fillets in skin-down and press each flat with a spatula for a few seconds.

💡Pressing stops the skin curling.
Step 5 of 8

Cook undisturbed until the skin releases cleanly from the pan and the flesh turns pale and opaque two-thirds of the way up the sides.

Step 6 of 8

Flip and cook just until the center gives softly when pressed, then move the fillets to plates skin-side up so the crust stays crackly.

Step 7 of 8

Drain the potatoes and return them to the hot dry pot, then crush each one flat with the back of a spoon and toss with the butter, the capers and more chopped dill until glossy.

Step 8 of 8

Dollop the yogurt over the potatoes, spoon the mustard-dill sauce generously over the salmon, and serve with the cold cucumbers and a lemon wedge.

🥪 Salvadoran Panes con Pollo
Step 1 of 8

Toast the pepitas and sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium, shaking often, until they pop and turn nut-brown and fragrant. Tip them onto a board and chop them fine, or crush them with the bottom of a mug.

💡This crushed seed paste is the relajo.
Step 2 of 8

Season the chicken thighs hard with salt and pepper. Add olive oil to the same skillet over medium-high and sear the thighs undisturbed until the undersides are deep mahogany.

Step 3 of 8

Flip the chicken, add the onion and garlic around it, and cook until the onion slumps and starts to take color in the rendered fat.

Step 4 of 8

Pour in the tomato sauce, the crushed seeds, the oregano, the cumin and 1/2 cup water. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook at a lazy bubble until the chicken pulls apart under a fork.

Step 5 of 8

While the chicken braises, toss the cabbage and radishes with a big pinch of salt and a splash of vinegar or lime, then press it down in the bowl and leave it to wilt and sharpen.

Step 6 of 8

Shred the chicken directly in the pan with two forks, then simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens enough to cling to the meat rather than run off it.

💡You want it saucy, not soupy.
Step 7 of 8

Split the brioche buns, spread the cut sides with mayonnaise, and toast them face-down in a dry skillet over medium until the edges are crisp and freckled brown.

Step 8 of 8

Pile the chicken onto the bottom buns, spoon extra sauce over so it soaks in, and crown with a tangle of the cabbage and radish before closing the sandwiches.

🐖 Goan Pork Vindaloo
Step 1 of 8

Whisk the vinegar, garlic, ginger, paprika, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, cayenne, brown sugar and a heavy pinch of salt into a loose rust-red paste. Toss the pork through it until every cube is coated and leave it to marinate while you chop the onion.

💡Vinegar first is what makes it vindaloo.
Step 2 of 8

Heat a film of olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high until it ripples. Lift the pork out of the marinade, letting the excess drip back into the bowl, and brown it in two uncrowded batches until each side is deeply crusted.

💡Crowding steams the meat.
Step 3 of 8

Set the pork aside and drop the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook, scraping the browned bits off the bottom, until it is soft and the edges are golden.

Step 4 of 8

Return the pork and every drop of the reserved marinade to the pot, pour in 1 cup water, and bring it to a strong bubble while you scrape the base clean one last time.

Step 5 of 8

Cover, lower the heat until the surface just shivers, and simmer until the pork surrenders to a fork with no resistance. Stir once halfway to keep the bottom from catching.

Step 6 of 8

While it simmers, heat the rice pouches and fluff them into a wide bowl with a fork so the grains stay separate.

Step 7 of 8

Uncover, raise the heat to medium, and reduce until the sauce clings to the pork and a slick of red-tinted oil rises to the surface.

💡The oil surfacing means it is done.
Step 8 of 8

Pull the pot off the heat and let it settle, then taste and adjust with salt or another splash of vinegar for brightness before spooning it over the basmati.

🧈 Chicken Kyiv Cutlets with Garlic-Dill Butter
Step 1 of 9

Mash the softened butter with the garlic, a fistful of chopped dill, salt and pepper. Roll it into two tight logs in plastic wrap and freeze until hard to the touch.

💡Rock-hard butter will not leak out while frying.
Step 2 of 9

Butterfly each breast almost in half and open it like a book, then pound it between two sheets of plastic until it is an even thin sheet with no thick lump in the middle.

Step 3 of 9

Lay a frozen butter log on each cutlet, fold the sides in, and roll it up into a tight parcel, pressing the seam and ends firmly closed so there is no gap.

💡Any gap is an escape route.
Step 4 of 9

Set out flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in three dishes. Roll each parcel through flour, then egg, then crumbs, then egg and crumbs a second time, pressing hard for a thick armored coating. Chill the breaded rolls while the oil heats.

Step 5 of 9

Heat about half an inch of oil in a deep skillet over medium until a dropped breadcrumb sizzles steadily on contact. Lower the rolls in seam-side down and fry, turning every couple of minutes, until every side is deep even gold.

Step 6 of 9

Move the cutlets to a rack set over a sheet pan and finish them in a 400F oven until the thickest part is firm and springy rather than squishy.

Step 7 of 9

While they finish, simmer the peas in salted water until bright green and just tender, then drain and toss them with chopped dill and a squeeze of lemon.

Step 8 of 9

Stir the sour cream with the mustard, a spoonful of lemon juice and more dill until it is pourable, and season it sharply.

Step 9 of 9

Rest the cutlets briefly so the butter stops boiling inside, then cut into them at the table and let the garlic butter flood the plate.

💡Cut at the table for the reveal.
🫓 Hawaij Chicken with Sahawiq and Charred Naan
Step 1 of 7

Whisk the cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, a very generous grind of black pepper, salt, two grated garlic cloves and olive oil into a thick hawaij rub. Massage it into the thighs and leave them out while the pan heats.

💡Black pepper is the backbone of hawaij.
Step 2 of 7

Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high until a drop of water skitters instantly. Lay the thighs in smooth-side down and leave them completely alone so the spices toast into a crust.

Step 3 of 7

Flip the chicken when the undersides are dark mahogany and cook until the thickest piece is firm and the juices run clear.

Step 4 of 7

While the chicken sears, make the sahawiq: chop the cilantro, chilies, remaining garlic and tomatoes together on a board until you have a rough, wet green-flecked relish, then season it hard with salt and lemon juice.

💡Chop, do not puree, for texture.
Step 5 of 7

Move the chicken to a board to rest, and while it does, press the naan into the spiced drippings in the hot pan until it puffs and the edges blacken in spots.

Step 6 of 7

Stir the lemon zest and a pinch of salt into the yogurt so it tastes bright rather than flat.

Step 7 of 7

Slice the chicken thickly against the grain, pile it onto the charred naan, and spoon over the sahawiq and cold yogurt just before eating.

🫘 Tuscan Rosemary Pork Chops with Cannellini and Kale
Step 1 of 8

Salt the chops aggressively on both sides and let them sit on the counter while you strip the kale and smash the garlic, so they lose their chill and the salt sinks in.

💡Room-temperature chops cook evenly.
Step 2 of 8

Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high with the olive oil until it shimmers and sends up a first wisp of smoke. Lay the chops in away from you and do not touch them until a hard dark crust forms underneath.

Step 3 of 8

Flip the chops and add the rosemary, sage and half the garlic to the pan. Tilt the skillet and spoon the sizzling herb oil over the meat continuously until the chops feel firm with a slight give near the bone.

💡Basting is what perfumes the meat.
Step 4 of 8

Move the chops to a board with the crisped herbs on top and let them rest while you build the beans in the same pan.

Step 5 of 8

Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining garlic and the red pepper flakes to the drippings, stirring until they sizzle steadily and smell sweet.

Step 6 of 8

Add the beans and the broth, then crush about a third of the beans against the side of the pan. Simmer until the liquid turns creamy and coats the whole spoon.

Step 7 of 8

Fold in the kale by the handful and cook until it collapses into glossy dark green ribbons and the pan is nearly dry again.

Step 8 of 8

Finish the beans with lemon juice and the parmesan, then spoon them onto plates, set the chops on top, and zigzag the balsamic glaze over everything.

🫒 Puerto Rican Carne Guisada with Olives and Potatoes
Step 1 of 9

Pat the beef dry and season it hard with salt, pepper and half the oregano. Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the cubes in two uncrowded batches until they are crusted on at least two sides.

💡Small cubes turn tender inside the short simmer.
Step 2 of 9

While the beef browns, pulse the onion, bell pepper, garlic and the cilantro stems in a food processor, or chop them very fine by hand, into a rough wet sofrito.

Step 3 of 9

Lift the beef out, drop the heat to medium, and add the sofrito to the drippings. Cook, scraping the fond up off the bottom, until the raw onion smell is gone and the mixture looks jammy rather than watery.

Step 4 of 9

Stir in the paprika and the remaining oregano for a few seconds, then add the tomato sauce and cook until it darkens to brick red and pulls away from the pan when you drag a spoon through.

Step 5 of 9

Return the beef and its juices, pour in the broth, and bring it to a bubble. Cover, drop the heat until the surface barely shivers, and simmer.

Step 6 of 9

Add the potatoes and olives, pushing them under the liquid, then cover again and simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender and the beef pulls apart under light pressure.

Step 7 of 9

Uncover, raise the heat to medium, and reduce until the gravy thickly coats a spoon and the potatoes sit half-submerged instead of swimming.

💡Some potato will break down and thicken it for you.
Step 8 of 9

While it reduces, heat the rice pouches and fluff them so the grains separate.

Step 9 of 9

Pull the pot off the heat, stir in a big handful of chopped cilantro leaves, and let it settle before ladling it over the rice.

🥢 Shanghai Red-Braised Chicken with Star Anise and Scallions
Step 1 of 8

Pat the chicken thoroughly dry. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high until it shimmers and thins out, then lay the thighs in a single layer and sear undisturbed until the undersides are deep golden and release from the pan without tugging.

💡Crowding steams the meat instead of browning it.
Step 2 of 8

Push the chicken to one side and drop the ginger coins, smashed garlic and scallion whites into the bare patch. Stir them in the hot fat until they smell sweet and toasty and the garlic edges turn pale gold.

Step 3 of 8

Pour in the soy sauce, sherry and brown sugar along with 1/2 cup water, then drop in the star anise. Scrape the browned bits off the bottom and bring everything to a hard, rolling bubble.

Step 4 of 8

Lower the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the chicken is fork-tender and the liquid has reduced by about half. Turn the pieces once halfway through so both sides take on color.

💡A lazy blip-blip bubble, not a boil.
Step 5 of 8

Nestle the bok choy halves cut-side down into the braising liquid and re-cover. Cook until the stems are crisp-tender and the leaves have collapsed and gone glossy dark green.

Step 6 of 8

While the bok choy steams, heat the frozen jasmine rice according to the bag and fluff it with a fork.

Step 7 of 8

Uncover, raise the heat to medium-high, and boil the sauce down, spooning it over the chicken, until it is syrupy and coats the back of a spoon in a thin sheet.

💡It thickens further off the heat, so pull it a touch loose.
Step 8 of 8

Kill the heat and swirl in the rice vinegar and sesame oil. Fish out the star anise, pile the chicken and bok choy over the rice, and shower with the raw scallion greens.

🐟 Bengali Shorshe Salmon in Mustard-Turmeric Sauce
Step 1 of 7

Rub the salmon all over with the turmeric and a generous pinch of salt and set it aside while you build the sauce.

💡The turmeric seasons the fish and stains it a deep marigold.
Step 2 of 7

Whisk both mustards with the sugar and 3/4 cup water until completely smooth and pourable, with no thick paste clinging to the whisk.

Step 3 of 7

Heat the mustard oil in a lidded skillet over medium-high until it just begins to wisp smoke, then cut the heat to medium and add the nigella seeds and slit chiles. They should crackle and sputter the instant they hit the oil.

💡Smoking the oil first burns off its raw pungency.
Step 4 of 7

Pour in the mustard slurry, stand back from the fumes, and simmer until it loses its raw bite and thickens just enough to leave a trail behind the spoon.

Step 5 of 7

Slide the salmon in, spoon sauce over the top, cover, and poach over medium-low until the fish flakes when nudged at the thickest part and the center has just turned matte.

Step 6 of 7

While the fish poaches, heat the basmati pouch and tear the cilantro.

Step 7 of 7

Take the pan off the heat, squeeze in half the lime, and let it stand uncovered so the sauce tightens around the fish. Serve over the rice with cilantro, the softened chiles, and the rest of the lime.

🍤 Catalan Romesco Shrimp with Blistered Scallions
Step 1 of 7

Warm 3 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium and fry one slice of bread, torn into rough pieces, together with the whole garlic cloves until both are golden brown and crisp at the edges.

💡Fried bread is what gives romesco its body.
Step 2 of 7

Scrape the bread and garlic into a food processor with the almonds, drained fire roasted peppers and onions, smoked paprika, sherry vinegar and crushed red pepper. Blitz to a coarse, spoonable sauce with visible flecks of almond, then season with salt.

Step 3 of 7

Wipe the skillet, set it over high heat, and lay the scallions in a single layer. Leave them alone until they blister and blacken in spots, then turn once and char the other side.

💡You want real black patches, not gentle browning.
Step 4 of 7

While the scallions char, pat the shrimp dry a second time and season them with salt.

💡Wet shrimp steam and turn rubbery.
Step 5 of 7

Pile the scallions onto a platter. Add a slick of oil to the ripping-hot pan and lay the shrimp down in one layer, searing undisturbed until the edges turn opaque pink and the bottoms curl.

Step 6 of 7

Flip and cook just until the shrimp are opaque through the middle and springy to the touch.

💡Argentinian reds cook fast; pull them early.
Step 7 of 7

Toast the remaining bread slice, squeeze lemon over the shrimp, and spoon a thick bed of romesco onto each plate. Drag the shrimp and scallions through it and finish with parsley.

🍛 Venezuelan Pabellon Bowls with Sweet Plantains
Step 1 of 8

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in your largest pot over medium-high. Add the onion, bell pepper and a big pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, until the vegetables slump completely and the edges catch brown.

💡This sofrito is the backbone of the dish, so let it go past merely soft.
Step 2 of 8

Push the sofrito to the rim, add the beef in the center, press it into a flat slab, and leave it untouched so it browns hard before you break it into crumbles.

Step 3 of 8

Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano and cook until the spices coat the meat and smell toasted rather than dusty.

Step 4 of 8

Add the tomatoes and Worcestershire, scrape the bottom clean, and simmer uncovered, stirring every few minutes, until the guiso is thick and glossy with no watery pool at the edges.

Step 5 of 8

While the beef simmers, heat the oven to 425F and tip the black beans with all their liquid into a saucepan. Season with salt and a pinch of cumin and simmer until brothy but slightly thickened, smashing a few beans against the side of the pot.

💡Those smashed beans give the pot body.
Step 6 of 8

Spread the frozen plantains on a sheet pan and roast, turning once, until the edges are dark, sticky and caramelized.

Step 7 of 8

Heat the rice pouches in the last few minutes and fluff them into a serving bowl.

Step 8 of 8

Build each bowl in stripes: rice, then guiso, then brothy beans, then plantains, and crumble the queso fresco over the top.

🌶️ Isan Pork Larb with Toasted Rice Powder
Step 1 of 7

Toast the raw rice in a dry skillet over medium, shaking the pan constantly, until every grain is the color of weak tea and the kitchen smells like popcorn.

💡This powder is the soul of larb, so do not skip it.
Step 2 of 7

Grind the toasted rice to a coarse sand in a mortar, spice grinder, or a zip-top bag under a rolling pin, then set it aside.

Step 3 of 7

Add 1/4 cup water to the same skillet over medium-high, drop in the pork, and mash it into fine crumbles with the back of a spoon. Cook until no pink remains but the meat still looks moist and loose.

💡The splash of water keeps the pork tender instead of crusty.
Step 4 of 7

While the pork cooks, slice the shallot and scallions, pick the mint leaves, and separate the cabbage leaves into a bowl of ice water so they go glassy and crisp.

Step 5 of 7

Kill the heat and pour in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chili flakes. Stir and taste: it should be aggressively sour, salty and hot, all at once.

💡Season while the pork is warm so it drinks the dressing in.
Step 6 of 7

Fold in the shallot, scallions, most of the herbs and all but a spoonful of the rice powder. The mixture should look glossy and clumped, never soupy.

Step 7 of 7

Pile the larb into a bowl, dust with the reserved rice powder and remaining herbs, and serve with the drained cabbage leaves and hot jasmine rice.

🥔 Danish Frikadeller with Dill Potatoes and Agurkesalat
Step 1 of 8

Put the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water, bring to a boil over high heat, then cook at a steady simmer until a knife slides into the largest one with no resistance.

Step 2 of 8

While the potatoes cook, toss the cucumber slices with the vinegar, sugar and 1/2 tsp salt and refrigerate. They will go limp and translucent and release a pool of sharp brine.

Step 3 of 8

Grate the onion straight into a bowl, juice and all, then add the pork, beef, egg, flour, allspice, 1 1/2 tsp salt and plenty of pepper. Beat hard with a wooden spoon until the mass turns pale, sticky and springy.

💡The beating is what gives frikadeller their bounce.
Step 4 of 8

Melt 3 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium until it foams. Scoop the meat with a spoon, shape ovals with a wet hand, and set them straight into the foaming butter.

💡Wet hands keep the mixture from gluing itself to you.
Step 5 of 8

Fry undisturbed until the undersides are deep mahogany and a spatula lifts them cleanly.

💡Keep it at medium; butter scorches above that.
Step 6 of 8

Flip and fry the second side until browned and firm when pressed, with no pink at the center of the thickest one.

Step 7 of 8

Drain the potatoes, return them to the hot dry pot, add the remaining butter and most of the dill, and swirl the pot until every potato glistens and a few skins split.

Step 8 of 8

Plate the frikadeller with the dill potatoes and a drained mound of the cucumber salad, then spoon the browned butter from the skillet over the top.

🥬 Guatemalan Pollo en Jocon
Step 1 of 8

Toast the pepitas and sesame seeds together in a dry skillet over medium, shaking often, until the pepitas puff and pop and the sesame turns gold.

💡Pull them the moment they smell nutty; they scorch in seconds.
Step 2 of 8

Blend the toasted seeds with the salsa verde, cilantro, scallions, bell pepper, garlic and coriander until completely smooth and shockingly bright green.

Step 3 of 8

Season the chicken thighs generously with salt. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high and sear them in a single layer until the undersides are well browned.

💡You are after color here, not doneness.
Step 4 of 8

Pour the green sauce over the chicken — it will hiss and spatter — then add the broth and scrape the bottom of the pot clean.

Step 5 of 8

Simmer uncovered over medium-low, stirring occasionally, until the sauce shifts from grass green to a deeper olive and thickens enough to coat the chicken.

💡That color change is your cue that the raw edge has cooked out.
Step 6 of 8

While it simmers, warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet until they puff, soften and speckle, then stack them inside a folded towel.

Step 7 of 8

Shred the chicken into big rough pieces with two forks right in the pot, stir it back through the sauce, and season with salt to taste.

Step 8 of 8

Heat the rice pouch, then ladle the jocon over it with the warm tortillas alongside for scooping.

🍗 Big-Batch Andalusian Sherry-Garlic Chicken with Saffron Potatoes
Step 1 of 9

Heat the oven to 400F. Pat the chicken bone-dry and salt it heavily on both sides, then let it sit uncovered while the oven comes up to temperature.

💡Dry skin is the only route to crisp skin.
Step 2 of 9

Crumble the saffron threads into 1/2 cup warm water and leave them to bloom into a deep orange infusion.

Step 3 of 9

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high and sear the chicken skin-side down in two batches until the skin is bronzed and lifts away without sticking.

💡Two unhurried batches beat one crowded, steamy one.
Step 4 of 9

Move the chicken to a plate. Pour off all but a slick of the fat, add the onion and smashed garlic, and cook over medium until the garlic is soft and golden through, stirring so nothing catches.

💡Burnt garlic will sour the whole pot.
Step 5 of 9

Stir in the cumin and bay leaves for a minute, then pour in the sherry and scrape up every browned bit. Boil hard until the sharp alcohol smell has burned off and the liquid looks syrupy.

Step 6 of 9

Add the potatoes and the saffron water, season with salt, and nestle the chicken back in skin-side up so the skin sits above the liquid.

Step 7 of 9

Slide the uncovered pot into the oven and roast until the potatoes are tender all the way through, the sauce has reduced around them, and the chicken pulls easily from the bone.

💡Baste the potatoes if you like, but never the skin.
Step 8 of 9

Scatter the olives over the top and return the pot to the oven just long enough to heat them through and soften them slightly.

Step 9 of 9

Off the heat, stir the sherry vinegar and lemon juice into the pan sauce, taste for salt, and finish with the lemon zest and parsley.

🔥 Hunan Farmhouse Pork with Blistered Green Chilies
Step 1 of 7

Put the pork in the freezer for 10 minutes to firm up, then slice it against the grain as thin as you can manage. Toss the slices with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and a heavy grind of black pepper.

💡Half-frozen meat is the only way to get paper-thin slices with a home knife.
Step 2 of 7

Set a carbon steel or heavy stainless skillet over your highest heat and let it preheat dry for 2 minutes, until the surface looks dull and the first wisp of smoke lifts off. Slice the chilies, garlic, and ginger while it heats.

💡Open a window before you blister chilies.
Step 3 of 7

Add a slick of oil and lay the pork out in a single layer. Sear undisturbed for 3 minutes, until the edges curl and the undersides are brown and lacquered, then toss once and scrape it onto a plate.

💡Two batches beats one crowded gray one.
Step 4 of 7

Add another spoonful of oil and dump in the chilies. Leave them mostly alone over high heat for 4 minutes, until the skins are streaked black and blistered and the flesh has slumped.

Step 5 of 7

Push the chilies to one side, add the garlic, ginger, and fermented black beans to the bare metal, and stir for 1 minute until the garlic goes pale gold and the whole pan smells salty and savory.

💡Any darker than gold and the garlic turns bitter.
Step 6 of 7

Return the pork and its juices, add the remaining soy sauce, the vinegar, and the sugar, and toss hard for 2 minutes until the liquid has nearly vanished and everything wears a glossy coat. Heat the jasmine rice in the microwave while you toss.

Step 7 of 7

Kill the heat and fold in the scallion batons and the Crunchy Chili Onion so the crunch survives. Pile it over the hot rice and spoon the pan drippings on top.

💡Adding chili onion off-heat keeps the fried garlic bits crisp.
🍛 Chettinad Pepper Chicken with Curry Leaves
Step 1 of 8

Toss the chicken with the yogurt, turmeric, half the chili powder, and a big pinch of salt until every piece is slicked yellow. Leave it on the counter for 10 minutes while you prep everything else.

Step 2 of 8

Toast the peppercorns, fennel, and coriander in a dry skillet over medium for 2 minutes, shaking constantly, until the fennel darkens a shade and the pepper smells sharp and piney. Crush them coarsely in a mortar or under the bottom of a heavy pan.

💡Coarse, not powdered — you want to bite into the pepper.
Step 3 of 8

Wipe the pan, add 2 tbsp coconut oil, and heat over medium-high. Strip in the curry leaves and stand back for 1 minute while they crackle, curl, and turn glassy.

Step 4 of 8

Add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until it collapses and the edges go deep brown. Crush the rest of your spices while you wait.

Step 5 of 8

Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and the remaining chili powder and cook 1 minute, until the raw garlic smell burns off and the oil at the edge of the pan turns red.

Step 6 of 8

Spread the marinated chicken into a single layer and leave it completely alone for 5 minutes, until the undersides are browned and release from the pan without tearing.

💡Resist stirring — that first sear is where the flavor lives.
Step 7 of 8

Add the tomato and two-thirds of the crushed pepper masala with a splash of water, cover, and cook 10 minutes until the tomato collapses into the sauce and the chicken is opaque throughout.

Step 8 of 8

Uncover, raise the heat, and cook 4 more minutes until the sauce is nearly dry and clinging to the meat. Off the heat, stir in the last of the pepper masala and warm the naan directly over the burner or in the hot pan.

💡Finishing with raw-toasted pepper keeps the heat bright instead of muddy.
🍅 Neapolitan Chicken Pizzaiola with Olives and Torn Mozzarella
Step 1 of 7

Pat the cutlets bone dry and season both sides hard with salt and pepper. Film a wide skillet with olive oil and heat over medium-high for 2 minutes, until the oil shimmers and thins out across the pan.

💡Dry chicken browns; damp chicken steams.
Step 2 of 7

Lay the cutlets in without crowding and sear 3 minutes, until the undersides are burnished gold and lift cleanly. Flip, give them 1 more minute, and move them to a plate — they should still be pink inside.

Step 3 of 7

Drop the heat to medium and add the garlic and pepper flakes to the browned fond. Stir for 1 minute, only until the garlic turns blond at the edges and smells sweet.

💡Browned garlic will make the whole sauce bitter.
Step 4 of 7

Crush the tomatoes into the pan through your fingers, add the oregano and a big pinch of salt, and simmer uncovered for 12 minutes. It's ready when it darkens to brick red and orange oil pools around the edge. Tear the mozzarella into rough pieces while it cooks.

💡Rubbing the dried oregano between your palms as it goes in wakes it up.
Step 5 of 7

Stir in the olives and capers, then taste for salt — between the two, it may need none at all.

Step 6 of 7

Nestle the cutlets and any collected juices back into the sauce, drape the torn mozzarella over the top, cover, and cook on low for 5 minutes until the cheese slumps into puddles and the chicken is opaque at its thickest point.

Step 7 of 7

Rest it off the heat for 3 minutes, then tear the basil over the top and drizzle with raw olive oil. Serve straight from the pan with torn ciabatta for the sauce.

🍗 Dominican Pollo Guisado with Green Olives
Step 1 of 8

Toss the chicken with the adobo seasoning, oregano, minced cilantro stems, the juice of one lime, salt, and pepper until every piece is coated. Let it sit for 15 minutes while you chop the garlic and potatoes.

💡Getting seasoning under the skin pays off later.
Step 2 of 8

Set a wide Dutch oven over medium heat with 2 tbsp oil and the sugar. Leave it alone for 3 minutes, swirling only once, until the sugar melts and turns the color of an old penny and smells like caramel.

💡Past dark amber it turns bitter — pull it the second it goes copper.
Step 3 of 8

Add the chicken skin-side down in batches without crowding and sear 5 minutes per batch, until the caramel and fat have lacquered the skin a glossy deep brown. Move each batch to a sheet pan.

Step 4 of 8

Dump the fire roasted peppers and onions straight from the bag into the pot and cook 5 minutes over medium-high, until their water boils off and they start to sizzle and catch color.

Step 5 of 8

Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, scraping constantly, until the paste darkens to brick and coats the vegetables.

Step 6 of 8

Return the chicken with any juices, add the olives and their brine, and pour in enough water to come halfway up the meat. Bring it to a boil, then drop to a bare simmer, cover, and cook 25 minutes.

Step 7 of 8

Add the potatoes, uncover, and simmer 20 minutes more, until a knife slides into a potato with no resistance and the sauce has reduced enough to coat the back of a spoon. Heat the rice pouches near the end.

💡Mash one potato into the sauce to thicken it fast.
Step 8 of 8

Pull it off the heat, squeeze in the second lime, and shower with the cilantro leaves. Let it settle for 10 minutes so the sauce tightens, then spoon it over the rice.

🥬 Laotian Larb Gai with Toasted Rice Powder
Step 1 of 7

Toast the raw rice in a dry skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes, shaking almost constantly, until every grain is the color of weak tea and the pan smells like popcorn. Tip it onto a plate to cool.

💡This is the whole dish — don't rush it pale.
Step 2 of 7

Grind the cooled rice to the texture of coarse sand in a mortar, spice grinder, or under a heavy pan on a cutting board.

Step 3 of 7

Add a few tablespoons of water and the ground chicken to the same skillet over medium-high and break it into fine crumbles with a spatula. Cook 7 minutes, until no pink remains and the liquid has mostly cooked off.

💡Poaching in a splash of water keeps the meat tender instead of pebbly.
Step 4 of 7

Kill the heat and let the chicken sit for 3 minutes so it stops steaming. Slice the shallots and scallions while you wait.

Step 5 of 7

Whisk the fish sauce, the juice of two limes, the sugar, and the chili flakes until the sugar dissolves. Taste it — it should hit sour first, salty second, hot last.

Step 6 of 7

Pour the dressing over the warm chicken and toss with the shallots and scallions until every crumble is coated and the shallots soften slightly.

Step 7 of 7

Fold in the mint, cilantro, and most of the rice powder right before you serve, then taste and correct with the last lime or more fish sauce. Pile it onto a platter with the lettuce leaves and cucumber spears and dust with the remaining rice powder.

💡Add the rice powder at the last second or it goes soggy.
🧆 Swedish Meatballs in Allspice Cream with Pickled Cucumber
Step 1 of 8

Shave the cucumber into near-transparent coins and toss with the vinegar, sugar, a big pinch of salt, and the chopped dill stems. Leave it to pickle for 20 minutes, tossing once, until the slices go limp and translucent.

Step 2 of 8

Soak the panko in 1/3 cup of the cream for 5 minutes, until it looks like wet sand and no dry crumbs remain.

💡This soaked-bread trick is what keeps them soft.
Step 3 of 8

Mix the beef, soaked panko, grated onion, allspice and nutmeg, and a generous amount of salt and pepper with your hands just until it comes together. Roll into about twenty walnut-sized balls with damp hands.

💡Overmixing makes them bouncy instead of tender.
Step 4 of 8

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter with a little oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and add the meatballs with space between them. Leave them undisturbed for 5 minutes, until a dark brown crust forms on the underside.

Step 5 of 8

Roll them around the pan and cook 5 minutes more, until browned on all sides and springy to a poke. Move them to a plate.

Step 6 of 8

Melt the remaining butter in the same pan over medium and whisk in the flour. Cook 2 minutes, whisking, until the paste turns pale tan and smells toasty rather than raw.

Step 7 of 8

Pour in the broth in a steady stream while whisking, then the rest of the cream. Simmer 5 minutes until it coats a spoon and a finger drawn across leaves a clean line.

💡If it tightens too much, loosen it with a splash of broth.
Step 8 of 8

Return the meatballs and any juices, cover, and simmer 5 minutes until cooked through and glossy. Shower with torn dill and serve with the drained pickles and a spoonful of jam on each plate.

🍳 Bolivian Silpancho with Fried Eggs and Llajua
Step 1 of 8

Make the llajua first: chop or briefly pulse the tomatoes, chiles, garlic, and half the cilantro into a loose, chunky salsa with the lime juice and plenty of salt. Let it sit and get juicy while you cook.

💡Leave the chile seeds in — llajua is supposed to bite.
Step 2 of 8

Lay each steak between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with the flat of a heavy pan until it's the thickness of a tortilla and nearly translucent at the edges. Season both sides with the cumin, salt, and pepper.

Step 3 of 8

Press each steak firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides so they stick in one solid layer, then set them on a rack while you cook the potatoes.

Step 4 of 8

Fry the potatoes in a film of oil in a large skillet over medium-high for 10 minutes, turning only two or three times, until they're deeply golden and crisp on the flat sides. Salt them and move them to a plate.

💡Turning them constantly is what keeps potatoes pale and soft.
Step 5 of 8

Add more oil to the same pan and fry the steaks one at a time over medium-high, 2 minutes per side, until the crust is crackly and deep golden. Slice the red onion thin while they cook.

Step 6 of 8

Heat the rice pouches, then fry the eggs in the same skillet over medium for 3 minutes, until the whites are set with lacy brown edges and the yolks still wobble.

Step 7 of 8

Press the hot rice into a small bowl and invert it onto each plate. Lay a steak alongside it and heap the crisp potatoes over the top.

Step 8 of 8

Crown each plate with two fried eggs, scatter the raw onion and remaining cilantro, and spoon llajua over everything. Break the yolks at the table and eat immediately.

🥣 Caldo Gallego with Chorizo, White Beans, and Greens
Step 1 of 8

Render the diced bacon in a large Dutch oven over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fat has pooled and the edges are browning. Lift it out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat behind.

Step 2 of 8

Season the pork hard with salt and pepper and brown it in the bacon fat in two batches, 5 minutes per batch, leaving it undisturbed until a real crust forms. Move it to a bowl.

💡Crowded pork boils in its own juice and never browns.
Step 3 of 8

Add the chorizo and cook 4 minutes, until the edges curl and the fat runs bright orange. Scoop it out and pour off all but about 2 tbsp of the fat.

💡That orange fat is the color of the whole soup — keep it.
Step 4 of 8

Cook the onions over medium for 8 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until soft and translucent. Stem and tear the greens while they cook.

Step 5 of 8

Pull the pot off the heat, add the garlic and pimenton, and stir for 1 minute so the paprika blooms in the hot fat without scorching.

💡Paprika burns in seconds over direct heat and turns acrid.
Step 6 of 8

Return the pork, bacon, and chorizo, add the broth and bay leaves, and bring to a boil. Drop to a low simmer, cover, and cook 25 minutes until the pork gives easily to a fork.

Step 7 of 8

Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until a knife tip slides through with no resistance and the broth has reduced slightly.

Step 8 of 8

Stir in the beans and the greens a handful at a time, then simmer 10 minutes until the greens are fully tender and the broth is cloudy and rich. Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot, fish out the bay leaves, and season with salt.

💡Mashing a little potato thickens it without any flour.
🍜 Beijing Zhajiangmian: Fried Bean Sauce Pork Noodles
Step 1 of 7

Whisk the hoisin, miso, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and 1/3 cup water in a bowl until completely smooth, then park it next to the stove. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the noodles.

💡Pre-mixing keeps the paste from scorching when it hits the pan.
Step 2 of 7

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or heavy skillet over medium-high until it shimmers, add the pork, and press it into one flat slab. Leave it completely alone until the underside is deep golden and crusted, then break it into rough crumbles.

💡Resist stirring, the crust is where the flavor comes from.
Step 3 of 7

Push the pork to one side, drop the scallion whites, garlic, and ginger into the rendered fat, and stir until fragrant and just softened. Fold everything together.

Step 4 of 7

Pour in the sauce, lower the heat to medium-low, and let it bubble lazily, stirring every couple of minutes, until it darkens to glossy mahogany and a slick of red oil separates around the edge. Cut the cucumber into matchsticks while it cooks.

💡Long and slow is what makes it taste roasted instead of raw.
Step 5 of 7

Boil the noodles until just chewy at the center, then scoop out 1/2 cup of the cooking water before draining. Rinse the noodles briefly under cold water so they stay bouncy.

Step 6 of 7

Stir the sesame oil and Crunchy Chili Onion into the sauce, then loosen it with splashes of noodle water until it slides off the spoon in a thick ribbon. Taste and add a pinch of salt only if it needs it, the miso is already salty.

Step 7 of 7

Divide the noodles between two deep bowls, spoon a generous mound of sauce into the center of each, and pile the cucumber and scallion greens around the rim. Bring them to the table unmixed and toss hard right before eating.

💡Mixing at the table is the tradition, not a shortcut.
🥣 Gujarati Kadhi with Crisped Paneer
Step 1 of 7

Whisk the yogurt, chickpea flour, turmeric, jaggery, 1 tsp salt, and 2 cups water in a bowl until it is absolutely lump-free and thin as heavy cream. Run your finger along the bottom of the bowl to check for hidden pockets of flour.

💡Any lump of besan will taste raw and chalky later.
Step 2 of 7

Pat the paneer dry and sear it in 1 tbsp of the ghee in a nonstick skillet over medium-high, turning once, until two sides are deep golden and the edges look crisp. Slide it onto a plate and salt it lightly.

💡Wet paneer will stick and tear instead of browning.
Step 3 of 7

Pour the yogurt mixture into a saucepan and bring it to a bare simmer over medium, whisking constantly in one direction until it thickens slightly and loses its raw, chalky smell.

💡Constant motion is what keeps the yogurt from splitting.
Step 4 of 7

Drop the heat to low and let it simmer uncovered, stirring every couple of minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon and tastes silky rather than floury. It should look like thin cream, not gravy.

Step 5 of 7

Make the vaghar: melt the remaining ghee in a small skillet over medium-high, add the mustard seeds, and hold a lid partly over the pan until they pop like rain against it.

💡Wait for the popping to slow, that is your cue.
Step 6 of 7

Add the cumin seeds, dried chiles, curry leaves, ginger, and asafoetida and stand back, the leaves will crackle violently. Swirl for about twenty seconds until everything smells nutty, then pour the whole spitting mixture straight into the kadhi.

💡Pour it in while it is still sizzling audibly.
Step 7 of 7

Taste for the Gujarati balance, sweet arriving first and sour right behind it, adjusting with a pinch more jaggery or salt. Heat the rice pouch, ladle the kadhi over it, add the paneer, and shower with cilantro.

🌿 Saltimbocca alla Romana with Skillet Artichokes
Step 1 of 7

Pound the cutlets between two sheets of plastic to an even 1/4 inch and season them with black pepper only, since the prosciutto brings plenty of salt. Lay two sage leaves on each, drape a slice of prosciutto over the top, and press it down firmly with your palm.

💡Even thickness means every cutlet finishes at the same moment.
Step 2 of 7

Dust only the bare chicken side in flour and shake off every bit of excess, leaving the prosciutto naked. Drain the artichokes and blot them dry on a towel while you work.

💡Flour on the ham would stop it from crisping.
Step 3 of 7

Heat 1 tbsp oil with 1 tbsp of the butter in a large skillet over medium-high until the foam subsides, then lay the cutlets in prosciutto side down. Cook without moving them until the ham is bronzed, crisp, and welded to the meat.

💡Press each cutlet gently for full contact.
Step 4 of 7

Flip and cook until the chicken is opaque and springs back when pressed, then move them to warm plates. Meanwhile set a second skillet over medium-high with 1 tbsp oil and the smashed garlic.

Step 5 of 7

Lay the artichokes cut side down in the second pan and leave them completely still until the flat faces are browned and blistered, then toss once and kill the heat.

💡They will spit, so keep a lid handy.
Step 6 of 7

Pour the wine into the empty chicken pan over medium-high and scrape up every brown fleck as it bubbles, reducing until it turns syrupy and just coats the back of a spoon.

Step 7 of 7

Pull the pan off the heat, swirl in the remaining butter and a squeeze of lemon until the sauce turns glossy, and spoon it over the cutlets. Toss the artichokes with the parsley, parmesan, and another squeeze of lemon and pile them alongside.

💡Off-heat butter is what makes the sauce shine instead of break.
🍗 Seco de Pollo: Ecuadorian Beer-Braised Chicken
Step 1 of 8

Blend the cilantro, garlic, beer, cumin, achiote, and 1 tsp salt until you have a smooth, violently green liquid. Pat the chicken bone dry and season it all over with salt and pepper.

💡Use the cilantro stems, they carry most of the flavor.
Step 2 of 8

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high until it shimmers, then brown the chicken skin side down in two batches without crowding, until the skin is deep gold and releases from the pot on its own. Move it to a plate.

💡If it sticks, it is not ready to turn.
Step 3 of 8

Pour off all but 2 tbsp of the fat, drop the heat to medium, and cook the yellow onions and bell pepper with a pinch of salt, scraping up the fond, until they are limp and edged with gold.

💡This refrito is the backbone of the whole pot.
Step 4 of 8

Add the tomatoes and brown sugar and cook, stirring often, until the tomatoes collapse and the mixture darkens and turns jammy enough to leave a trail behind the spoon.

Step 5 of 8

Pour in the green blend and bring it to a simmer, then nestle the chicken back in skin side up along with any juices from the plate. It will look alarmingly bright, but it dulls to olive as it cooks.

Step 6 of 8

Cover partially and simmer over low, adjusting the flame so the surface only blips, until the meat pulls away from the bone with a fork. While it braises, toss the sliced red onion with the juice of 2 limes and a big pinch of salt so it softens and turns pink.

💡A hard boil will toughen the chicken and dull the herbs.
Step 7 of 8

Uncover, raise the heat to medium, and reduce until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to cling to the pieces rather than pool around them. Taste and correct with salt and a squeeze of lime.

Step 8 of 8

Heat the rice pouches and serve the chicken over rice with plenty of sauce spooned across, topped with the pickled onions and the remaining lime cut into wedges.

💡The acid on top is what keeps the rich sauce moving.
🥩 Beef Lok Lak with Tuk Meric
Step 1 of 7

Toss the beef with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, half the garlic, and 1 tbsp of the cracked pepper until every cube is slick. Let it sit at room temperature while you build the rest.

💡Cracked, not ground, so you get gritty pops of pepper.
Step 2 of 7

Make the tuk meric by stirring the juice of 2 limes with the remaining cracked pepper, remaining garlic, and 1 tsp salt in a small bowl. Taste it, it should be aggressively sour, salty, and hot enough to make you blink.

💡This dip is the dish, do not tone it down.
Step 3 of 7

Line two plates with the lettuce, sliced tomato, and red onion and squeeze half a lime over the top. Heat the rice pouch and keep it covered.

Step 4 of 7

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a cast iron skillet over high until it is faintly smoking, then add half the beef in a single layer. Leave it untouched until a dark crust forms on the underside, toss for thirty seconds, and move it to a plate.

💡Two batches, or the beef steams and goes gray.
Step 5 of 7

Repeat with the second half of the beef, then return the first batch and all its juices and toss over high heat until the marinade reduces to a sticky glaze clinging to every cube.

Step 6 of 7

Wipe the skillet, add the remaining oil over medium-high, and fry the eggs until the whites are set with brown lacy edges but the yolks still wobble.

💡The running yolk becomes part of the sauce.
Step 7 of 7

Pile the beef over the salad, slide an egg onto each plate, and serve with rice and the tuk meric alongside for dipping bite by bite.

🥘 Kure na Paprice: Czech Paprika Cream Chicken
Step 1 of 8
